(August 2023) (Learn how and when to remove this message) Shillong was the capital of composite Assam during the British regime and for a quarter century in independent India until a separate State of Meghalaya was formed 1972. David Scott, the British civil servant of the East India Company, was the Agent of the Governor-General North East Frontier. During the First Anglo-Burmese War the British authorities felt the need for a road to connect Sylhet and Assam. The route was to traverse across the Khasi and Jaintia Hills. David Scott overcame the difficulties his administration faced from the opposition of the Khasi Syiems – their chiefs and people. Impressed by the favourable cool climate of Khasi Hills, they negotiated with the Syiem of Sohra in 1829 for a sanatorium for the British. Thus began the consolidation of British interests in the Khasi-Jaintia Hills. In early 1829, a Khasis confederation mounted a serious uprising against British occupation. But by January 1833, their leader Tirot Sing surrendered to David Scott and was detained to Dacca (present-day Dhaka). A political agent was posted in Sohra, also known as Cherrapunjee. But the British did not like the climate and facilities of Sohra and they moved to Shillong. "Ïewduh" is the biggest market in Shillong. The name "Shillong" was later adopted, as the location of the new town was below the Shillong Peak. In 1874, a separate Chief Commissionership was formed with Shillong as the seat of administration. The new administration included Sylhet, now a part of Bangladesh. Also included in the Chief Commissionership were the Naga Hills (present-day Nagaland), Lushai Hills (present-day Mizoram) as well as Khasi, Jaintia and Garo Hills. Shillong was the capital of composite Assam till 1969 when the autonomous state of Meghalaya was formed. In January 1972, Meghalaya was made a full-fledged state.[1] The Shillong Municipal Board dates back to 1878, when a proclamation was issued constituting Shillong and its suburbs, including the villages of Mawkhar and Laban, into a station under the Bengal Municipal Act of 1876. Inclusion of the villages of Mawkhar (S.E. Mawkhar, Jaiaw and part of Jhalupara and Mawprem) and Laban (Lumparing, Madan laban, Kench's Trace and Rilbong) within the Municipality of Shillong was agreed to by Haiñ Manik Syiem of Mylliem under the agreement of 15 November 1878.[2] But, there is no trace of Shillong in the British era maps dating back to 1878, up to 1900. The great earthquake of 12 June 1897 of moment magnitude 8.1 killed 27 from Shillong and destroyed much of the town. ^ .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output .citation q{quotes:"\"""\"""'""'"}.mw-parser-output .citation:target{background-color:rgba(0,127,255,0.133)}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-free.id-lock-free a{background:url("//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/65/Lock-green.svg")right 0.1em center/9px no-repeat}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-limited.id-lock-limited a,.mw-parser-output .id-lock-registration.id-lock-registration a{background:url("//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d6/Lock-gray-alt-2.svg")right 0.1em center/9px no-repeat}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-subscription.id-lock-subscripti

The observatory was built in 1442 during the Ming dynasty, and expanded during the Qing. It received major reorganization and many new, more accurate instruments from Europeans (Jesuits) in 1644.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] An image of the observatory after reorganization by the Jesuits The layout of the observatory It was said that in 1227, the Jin dynasty transferred the ancient astronomical instruments from Kaifeng to the first observatory in Beijing. In 1279, the succeeding Mongols under Kublai Khan built a new observatory just north of the current observatory. Kublai Khan made his chief adviser of hydraulics, mathematics and astronomy, Guo Shoujing, director of the observatory in 1283 after the death of Guo's friend and predecessor Zhang Wenqian.[1] After the Mongols, Zhu Yuanzhang, the founding Ming Emperor, transferred the instruments from Beijing to Nanjing. When the Yongle Emperor came to power, he had craftsmen make copies of the instruments in Nanjing and sent them to the Beijing observatory. The current observatory was completed in 1442. It assisted the Ming and Qing astronomers in their observation reports for the Emperor. As he was considered the "Son of Heaven", the movements of the heavenly bodies were an important affair. Another function was to assist sea navigation, with Muslim scholars recruited for their expertise in the area.[citation needed] In the mid-17th century, after winning an astronomy contest, the Jesuit Ferdinand Verbiest was awarded complete charge of the astronomy observatory by the emperor. In 1673, he supervised the rebuilding of some of the instruments. He and other Jesuits helped to further develop the observations of the stars and the planets. During the later stages of the Qing dynasty, members of the Eight-Nation Alliance looted some of the instruments. However, as World War I drew to a close, the instruments were returned to China by the French and German governments. An early seismograph of Zhang Heng's design used to be housed at the observatory. Some of the instruments from the Ming era are now at Purple Mountain Observatory in Nanjing.[2][3] ^ .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output .citation sections.content: Access and nearby attractions[edit] The Beijing Ancient Observatory is located just south of Jianguomen in Dongcheng District and can be accessed by Lines 1 and 2 of the Beijing Subway to Jianguomen station (Exit C) and bus routes 25, 39, 43, 44, 52, 122, 434, 637, 638, 750 and 特2 to Jianguomen South (建国门桥南). The Beijing railway station and the Ming City Wall Relics Park are a short walk to the south.

wikipedia.title: Rupnagar
wikipedia.extract: Rupnagar is a city and a municipal council in Rupnagar district in the Indian state of Punjab. Rupnagar is a newly created fifth Divisional Headquarters of Punjab comprising Rupnagar, Mohali, and its adjoining districts. It is also one of the bigger sites belonging to the Indus Valley civilization. Rupnagar is nearly 47 km (29 mi) to the northwest of Chandigarh and nearly 36 kilometres (22 mi) from Baddi- Barotiwala- Nalagarh (BBN) industrial corridor in Solan district of Himachal Pradesh. It is bordered by Himachal Pradesh to the north and Shahid Bhagat Singh Nagar district to its west.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] Etymology[edit] The ancient town of Rupnagar is said to have been named by a Raja called Rokeshar, who ruled during the 11th century and named it after his son Rup Sen.[1] Indus Valley civilization[edit] Indus Civilization site, Rupnagar (Ropar), Punjab, India Source:[2] Rupnagar is one of the Indus Valley sites along the Ghaggar-Hakra beds.[3] There is an Archaeological Museum[4] in the city which was opened in the year 1998 for general public. The museum exhibits the archaeological remains of excavated site in the city, the first Harappan site of Independent India.[5] These excavations reveal a cultural sequence from Harappan to medieval times. Some of the important exhibits include antiquities of Harappan times, gold coins of Chandragupta and copper and bronze implements.[5] ^ .mw-parser-output wikipedia.extract: Shillong is a hill station and the capital of Meghalaya, India. It is the headquarters of the East Khasi Hills district. Shillong is the 330th most populous city in India with a population of 143,229 according to the 2011 census. It is said that the rolling hills around the town reminded the British of Scotland. Hence, they would refer to it as the "Scotland of the East".

(August 2023) (Learn how and when to remove this message) Shillong was the capital of composite Assam during the British regime and for a quarter century in independent India until a separate State of Meghalaya was formed 1972. David Scott, the British civil servant of the East India Company, was the Agent of the Governor-General North East Frontier. During the First Anglo-Burmese War the British authorities felt the need for a road to connect Sylhet and Assam. The route was to traverse across the Khasi and Jaintia Hills. David Scott overcame the difficulties his administration faced from the opposition of the Khasi Syiems – their chiefs and people. Impressed by the favourable cool climate of Khasi Hills, they negotiated with the Syiem of Sohra in 1829 for a sanatorium for the British. Thus began the consolidation of British interests in the Khasi-Jaintia Hills. In early 1829, a Khasis confederation mounted a serious uprising against British occupation. But by January 1833, their leader Tirot Sing surrendered to David Scott and was detained to Dacca (present-day Dhaka). A political agent was posted in Sohra, also known as Cherrapunjee. But the British did not like the climate and facilities of Sohra and they moved to Shillong. "Ïewduh" is the biggest market in Shillong. The name "Shillong" was later adopted, as the location of the new town was below the Shillong Peak. In 1874, a separate Chief Commissionership was formed with Shillong as the seat of administration. The new administration included Sylhet, now a part of Bangladesh. Also included in the Chief Commissionership were the Naga Hills (present-day Nagaland), Lushai Hills (present-day Mizoram) as well as Khasi, Jaintia and Garo Hills. Shillong was the capital of composite Assam till 1969 when the autonomous state of Meghalaya was formed. In January 1972, Meghalaya was made a full-fledged state.[1] The Shillong Municipal Board dates back to 1878, when a proclamation was issued constituting Shillong and its suburbs, including the villages of Mawkhar and Laban, into a station under the Bengal Municipal Act of 1876. Inclusion of the villages of Mawkhar (S.E. Mawkhar, Jaiaw and part of Jhalupara and Mawprem) and Laban (Lumparing, Madan laban, Kench's Trace and Rilbong) within the Municipality of Shillong was agreed to by Haiñ Manik Syiem of Mylliem under the agreement of 15 November 1878.[2] But, there is no trace of Shillong in the British era maps dating back to 1878, up to 1900. The great earthquake of 12 June 1897 of moment magnitude 8.1 killed 27 from Shillong and destroyed much of the town. ^ .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output .citation q{quotes:"\"""\"""'""'"}.mw-parser-output .citation:target{background-color:rgba(0,127,255,0.133)}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-free.id-lock-free a{background:url("//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/65/Lock-green.svg")right 0.1em center/9px no-repeat}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-limited.id-lock-limited a,.mw-parser-output .id-lock-registration.id-lock-registration a{background:url("//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d6/Lock-gray-alt-2.svg")right 0.1em center/9px no-repeat}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-subscription.id-lock-subscripti

wikipedia.title: 北京古观象台
wikipedia.extract: The Beijing Ancient Observatory is a pretelescopic observatory located in Beijing, China. The observatory was built in 1442 during the Ming dynasty, and expanded during the Qing. It received major reorganization and many new, more accurate instruments from Europeans (Jesuits) in 1644.
wikipedia.extract_text: The Beijing Ancient Observatory is a pretelescopic observatory located in Beijing, China. The observatory was built in 1442 during the Ming dynasty, and expanded during the Qing. It received major reorganization and many new, more accurate instruments from Europeans (Jesuits) in 1644.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] An image of the observatory after reorganization by the Jesuits The layout of the observatory It was said that in 1227, the Jin dynasty transferred the ancient astronomical instruments from Kaifeng to the first observatory in Beijing. In 1279, the succeeding Mongols under Kublai Khan built a new observatory just north of the current observatory. Kublai Khan made his chief adviser of hydraulics, mathematics and astronomy, Guo Shoujing, director of the observatory in 1283 after the death of Guo's friend and predecessor Zhang Wenqian.[1] After the Mongols, Zhu Yuanzhang, the founding Ming Emperor, transferred the instruments from Beijing to Nanjing. When the Yongle Emperor came to power, he had craftsmen make copies of the instruments in Nanjing and sent them to the Beijing observatory. The current observatory was completed in 1442. It assisted the Ming and Qing astronomers in their observation reports for the Emperor. As he was considered the "Son of Heaven", the movements of the heavenly bodies were an important affair. Another function was to assist sea navigation, with Muslim scholars recruited for their expertise in the area.[citation needed] In the mid-17th century, after winning an astronomy contest, the Jesuit Ferdinand Verbiest was awarded complete charge of the astronomy observatory by the emperor. In 1673, he supervised the rebuilding of some of the instruments. He and other Jesuits helped to further develop the observations of the stars and the planets. During the later stages of the Qing dynasty, members of the Eight-Nation Alliance looted some of the instruments. However, as World War I drew to a close, the instruments were returned to China by the French and German governments. An early seismograph of Zhang Heng's design used to be housed at the observatory. Some of the instruments from the Ming era are now at Purple Mountain Observatory in Nanjing.[2][3] ^ .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output .citation sections.title: Access and nearby attractions
sections.content: Access and nearby attractions[edit] The Beijing Ancient Observatory is located just south of Jianguomen in Dongcheng District and can be accessed by Lines 1 and 2 of the Beijing Subway to Jianguomen station (Exit C) and bus routes 25, 39, 43, 44, 52, 122, 434, 637, 638, 750 and 特2 to Jianguomen South (建国门桥南). The Beijing railway station and the Ming City Wall Relics Park are a short walk to the south.

answer:
**Elephant Trunk Hill (象鼻山)** is a prominent landmark and tourist attraction located in **Guilin, Guangxi, China**. It is renowned for its unique shape that resembles an elephant drinking water. The site also features the **Water-Moon Cave**, where the moon's reflection creates a stunning visual effect, making it a popular spot for visitors.

### Key Information:
- **Name**: Elephant Trunk Hill (象鼻山)
- **Location**: Guilin, Guangxi, China
- **Category**: Attraction
- **Popularity**: Moderate (score: 0.7)
- **Visual Tags**: 
  - Exterior
  - Panoramic
  - Ground Level
  - Cityscape
  - Lake
  - Cave
  - Monument
  - Valley

### Historical Summary:
The Elephant Trunk Hill is recognized as a symbol of the city of Guilin. The round opening beneath the elephant's trunk is known as the Water-Moon Cave, which is particularly beautiful at night when the moon's reflection can be seen through the arch.

### Additional Information:
- For more details, you can visit the [Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elephant_Trunk_Hill).
- The hill is located at the confluence of the Taohua River and the Lijiang River, enhancing its scenic beauty.

If you have any specific questions or need further information, feel free to ask!

sections.title: Name
sections.content: Name[edit] Elephant Trunk Hill is the symbol of the city of Guilin. It got its name because it looks like an elephant drinking water.[1] The round opening that would be under the elephant’s trunk is known as Water-Moon Cave because at night the reflection of the moon can be seen through the arch and it looks as if it is under the water and floating on the surface of the water at the same time. Elephant Trunk Hill and Water-Moon Cave are located at the confluence of the Taohua River and the Lijiang River.[2] ^ .mw-parser-output Ulsanbawi is a must-visit for those looking to experience the natural beauty of South Korea, especially during the summer when the landscape is lush and vibrant. The viewpoint is accessible via hiking trails, making it an ideal spot for outdoor activities.

If you're planning a visit, be sure to enjoy the breathtaking views and the refreshing summer atmosphere!

result.llm_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT ve.viewpoint_id, 
                ve.name_primary, 
                ve.name_variants, 
                ve.category_norm, 
                ve.popularity, 
                1.0 AS name_score,

                1.0 AS category_score
FROM viewpoint_entity ve

JOIN viewpoint_visual_tags vt ON ve.viewpoint_id = vt.viewpoint_id

  AND w.extract_text ILIKE %s
  AND vca.viewpoint_country ILIKE %s
  AND vt.season = %s
ORDER BY ve.popularity DESC
LIMIT %s

query: The Mogao Caves, also known as the Thousand Buddha Grottoes, are a system of 500 temples located near Dunhuang, China. They were constructed starting in the 4th century AD and are renowned for their exquisite Buddhist art and frescoes, making them one of the largest repositories of Buddhist art in the world.
answer:
Here are some notable attractions related to the Mogao Caves, also known as the Thousand Buddha Grottoes, located in Dunhuang, China:

1. **莫高窟 (Mogao Caves)**
   - **Description**: The Mogao Caves, also known as the Thousand Buddha Grottoes, form a system of 500 temples located about 25 km southeast of Dunhuang. They are renowned for their exquisite Buddhist art and frescoes, making them one of the largest repositories of Buddhist art in the world.
   - **Historical Significance**: The caves contain some of the finest examples of Buddhist art spanning a period of 1,000 years.
   - **Visual Tags**: Cave, temple, China, panoramic, sunny.
   - **[More Info](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mogao_Caves)**

2. **吐峪溝石窟 (Tuyoq Thousand Buddha Caves)**
   - **Description**: This site features ancient cave temples and is recognized for its historical and cultural significance.
   - **Visual Tags**: Exterior, panoramic, mountain, cave, temple.
   - **[More Info](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuyoq_Thousand_Buddha_Caves)**

3. **麦积山石窟 (Maijishan Grottoes)**
   - **Description**: A series of 194 rock-cut caves located in Tianshui, Gansu Province, which contain over 7,200 Buddhist sculptures and murals.
   - **Visual Tags**: Mountain, cave, China, panoramic, sunny.
   - **[More Info](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maijishan_Grottoes)**

4. **马蹄寺石窟群 (Horse Hoof Temple Grottoes)**
   - **Description**: This site includes several caves and has historical significance dating back to the period of the Five Barbarians and the Sixteen Kingdoms.
   - **Visual Tags**: Exterior, panoramic, mountain, cave, temple.
   - **[More Info](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse_Hoof_Temple_Grottoes)**

5. **天梯山石窟 (Tiantishan Caves)**
   - **Description**: A series of rock-cut Buddhist cave temples located in the Liangzhou District of Wuwei, Gansu, with a history of excavation and decoration spanning several dynasties.
   - **Visual Tags**: Mountain, cave, China, panoramic, sunny.
   - **[More Info](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiantishan_Caves)**

These sites are rich in history and culture, showcasing the artistic achievements of Buddhist traditions in China. If you need more detailed information about any specific site, feel free to ask!

- **Opening Year**: The park opened in 1996.
- **Size**: It spans an impressive 36.5 hectares.
- **Location**: Situated in Ibusuki City, specifically at Yamakawa Okagamisui 1611.
- **Accessibility**: The nearest train station is Nishioyama Station, which is about a 35-minute walk away. It is also accessible by car from Yamakawa Station (approximately 15 minutes) and Ibusuki Station (approximately 25 minutes).
- **Opening Hours**: The park is open year-round, except for December 30 and 31.

### Visual Tags
The park is known for its blooming flowers and lush greenery, especially during the spring and summer seasons.

query: The Grand Buddha at Ling Shan is located near Wuxi, Jiangsu, on the north shore of Lake Tai. It is one of the largest Buddha statues in China and the world.

The Grand Buddha at Ling Shan, known as **灵山大佛**, is located near Wuxi, Jiangsu, on the north shore of Lake Tai. It is one of the largest Buddha statues in China and the world. Here are some details about this impressive attraction:

### Grand Buddha at Ling Shan (灵山大佛)
- **Category:** Attraction
- **Location:** Near Wuxi, Jiangsu, China
- **Description:** The Grand Buddha is situated within the Lingshan Scenic Area and is renowned for its monumental size and spiritual significance. It attracts many visitors who come to admire its grandeur and the surrounding natural beauty of Lake Tai.
- **Historical Summary:** The Grand Buddha is located on the north shore of Lake Tai, near Wuxi, Jiangsu, within the Lingshan Scenic Area. It is recognized as one of the largest Buddha statues in both China and the world.
- **Visual Tags:** The site is characterized by various visual tags such as "exterior," "panoramic," "temple," "lake," and "monument," indicating its scenic and architectural significance.

### Additional Information
- **Popularity:** The Grand Buddha is a well-known tourist destination, making it a popular spot for both local and international visitors.
- **Nearby Attractions:** The area around Lake Tai offers other scenic spots and cultural sites, enhancing the overall experience for tourists.

If you have any specific questions or need further information about visiting the Grand Buddha at Ling Shan, feel free to ask!

query: The Leshan Giant Buddha is a 71-meter tall stone statue carved into a cliff face, located at the confluence of the Min and Dadu Rivers in Sichuan Province, China. It is the largest and tallest stone Buddha statue in the world, facing Mount Emei.
answer:
Here are some details about the **Leshan Giant Buddha** and similar attractions:

### 1. Leshan Giant Buddha (乐山大佛)
- **Height**: 71 meters (233 ft)
- **Location**: At the confluence of the Min River and Dadu River in Sichuan Province, China.
- **Historical Summary**: The Leshan Giant Buddha is the largest and tallest stone Buddha statue in the world, built between 713 and 803 AD. It is carved out of a cliff face of Cretaceous red bed sandstones. The statue faces Mount Emei, with the rivers flowing below its feet.
- **Visual Tags**: 
  - Tags include: temple, monument, China, panoramic, sunny, crowded.
- **Historical Evidence**: 
  - [Wikipedia Reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/乐山大佛): "The Leshan Giant Buddha is a 71-meter (233 ft) tall stone statue, built between 713 and 803..."

### 2. Grand Buddha at Ling Shan (灵山大佛)
- **Location**: Near Wuxi, Jiangsu, within the Lingshan Scenic Area.
- **Historical Summary**: One of the largest Buddha statues in China and the world.
- **Visual Tags**: 
  - Tags include: exterior, panoramic, temple, lake, monument, China.
- **Historical Evidence**: 
  - [Wikipedia Reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/灵山大佛): "The Grand Buddha is located on the north shore of Lake Tai..."

### Summary
The **Leshan Giant Buddha** is a remarkable monument and a must-visit attraction in Sichuan Province, China. It stands as a testament to ancient artistry and religious significance. If you are interested in visiting or learning more about similar attractions, the Grand Buddha at Ling Shan is another notable site worth considering.

- **Historical Summary**: Wanping Fortress, also known as Wanping Castle, is a Ming Dynasty fortress or "walled city" in Fengtai District, Beijing. It was erected between 1638 and 1640 to defend Beijing against uprisings, particularly against Li Zicheng and his peasant uprising.

- **Source**: [Wikipedia](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A4%A7%E6%B0%B4%E6%B3%95)

### 3. **Deekshabhoomi**
- **Historical Summary**: A sacred monument of Navayana Buddhism located in Nagpur, India, where B. R. Ambedkar and approximately 400,000 followers embraced Buddhism.
- **Visual Tags**:

### 4. **War Memorial, Batasia Loop**
- **Historical Summary**: This memorial commemorates the sacrifices of soldiers and offers scenic views of the surrounding landscape.
- **Visual Tags**: 
  - Tags include: exterior, panoramic, mountain, cityscape, monument.
- **Source**: AI summary.

### 5. **象鼻山 (Elephant Trunk Hill)**
- **Historical Summary**: A landmark and tourist attraction in Guilin, Guangxi, China.
- **Visual Tags**: 
  - Tags include: exterior, panoramic, ground level, cityscape, lake, cave, monument.
- **Source**: [Wikipedia](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%B1%A1%E9%BC%BB%E5%B1%B1)

   - **Visual Tags**: Monument, temple, cityscape.

4. **War Memorial, Batasia Loop**
   - **Category**: Attraction
   - **Popularity**: 0.7
   - **Description**: A memorial commemorating soldiers, offering scenic views of the surrounding landscape.
   - **Visual Tags**: Monument, mountain, cityscape.

5. **象鼻山 (Elephant Trunk Hill)**
   - **Category**: Attraction
   - **Popularity**: 0.7
   - **Description**: A landmark in Guilin, Guangxi, China, known for its distinctive elephant trunk shape.
   - **Visual Tags**: Monument, lake, valley.

### Conclusion
The Zhuhai Fisher Girl is a unique cultural landmark, and while there are many other attractions nearby, none quite match its significance in Zhuhai. query: Тавдинские пещеры, located in the Altai region, are a large system of karst caves named after the nearby village of Tavda. The caves extend approximately 5 km and are popular among tourists, with some entrances equipped for easy access.
answer:
**Тавдинские пещеры** (или Талдинские пещеры) — это массив из большого числа карстовых пещер, расположенных в Алтайском районе Алтайского края, на левом берегу реки Катунь. Они получили свое название от деревни Тавда, которая раньше находилась неподалеку. Протяженность пещер составляет около 5 км, и они являются популярным туристическим направлением.

### Основные характеристики:
- **Легкий доступ**: Входы в пещеры находятся в отвесных скалах и утесах, многие из которых легко доступны. Некоторые входы оборудованы деревянными ступенями и освещены.
- **Система пещер**: Пещеры имеют несколько входов и соединяются друг с другом, образуя обширную взаимосвязанную систему.
- **Платный вход**: Вход в легкодоступные пещеры оборудован турникетами и является платным.

### Интересные факты:
- **Большая Тавдинская пещера** — это наиболее посещаемая пещера в массиве, известная своими археологическими находками, включая предметы гончарного производства и рыболовные принадлежности.
- **Тавдинская карстовая арка** — уникальная форма, представляющая остаток свода карстового туннеля, находящаяся на высоте около 80 метров над уровнем реки.

### Дополнительная информация:
- Для получения более подробной информации вы можете посетить [страницу на Википедии](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A2%D0%B0%D0%B2%D0%B4%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B5_%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%89%D0%B5%D1%80%D1%8B).

Тавдинские пещеры — это не только природное чудо, но и важный объект для изучения истории и археологии региона.

(7 марта 2025) Пещера под названием «Большая Тавдинская» (другие названия этой пещеры — «Девичьи слёзы», «Тавдинская-1») — это наиболее посещаемая туристами пещера в Тавдинском массиве. Нижние входы в неё находятся в 70-80 м от дороги и видны в просветы между деревьями. Главная галерея довольно просторна и постепенно поднимается. wikipedia.title: Тавдинские_пещеры
wikipedia.extract: Тавдинские или Талдинские пещеры — массив из большого числа пещер карстового происхождения в Алтайском районе Алтайского края, на левом берегу Катуни. Своё название пещеры получили от названия деревни Тавда, ранее располагавшейся неподалёку от этих мест. Протяжённость скал с пещерами составляет около 5 км. Входы в пещеры находятся в отвесных скалах и утесах, большая часть из которых легко доступна. В связи с популярностью и большой посещаемостью этого места туристами, некоторые входы даже оборудованы деревянными ступенями, в самые посещаемые туристами пещеры проведён свет. Многие пещеры имеют по несколько входов и соединяются друг с другом, образуя большую взаимосвязанную систему. Вход в легкодоступные пещеры оборудован турникетами и является платным.

На последнем 40-метровом участке, перед самым высшим входом, галерея, возвышаясь, закручивается спиралью, перекрывая свою нижнюю часть и образуя уступ. Она представляет редкую форму — остаток свода карстового туннеля или пещеры, имевший первоначально вид широкого пролёта — моста, а позднее — арки. Свод арки, толщиной 5 метров, покрыт редкой травяной растительностью и соснами. С 1996 г. Тавдинская карстовая арка имеет статус памятника природы.

wikipedia.title: 성산일출봉
wikipedia.extract: Seongsan Ilchulbong (Korean: 성산일출봉), also called Sunrise Peak, is a volcano on eastern Jeju Island, in Seongsan-ri, Seogwipo, Jeju Province, South Korea. It is 182 meters high and has a volcanic crater at the top.
wikipedia.extract_text: Seongsan Ilchulbong (Korean: 성산일출봉), also called Sunrise Peak, is a volcano on eastern Jeju Island, in Seongsan-ri, Seogwipo, Jeju Province, South Korea. It is 182 meters high and has a volcanic crater at the top.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: Description[edit] In 2021, a study reported that a 600 m (2,000 ft) wide crater from before the formation of Seongsan Ilchulbong now partially overlaps with the mountain site.[1] View of the mountain from space (2015) Seongsan Ilchulbong was formed around 6,700 years ago,[2] by Surtseyan-type hydrovolcanic activity upon a shallow seabed.[3][2] The earliest eruption related to the peak occurred around 600 m (2,000 ft) to the east of the current crater. After the eruption stopped, magma could not flow through that spot, which caused magma to later emerge at the location of the peak. Over time, most of the early cones and parts of the later tuff cone were eroded by waves, leaving parts of the internal structure exposed along the cliffs.[4] The mountain was originally disconnected from Jeju Island, but the accumulation of sediment caused the two to connect.[4][5] The mountain is considered to be geologically interesting and is actively studied by volcanologists.[6][5] The mountain is 182 m (597 ft) tall and has a diameter of 600 m (2,000 ft). It has a grassy volcanic crater at the top with a smooth, shallow bowl shape. The crater has an area of 2.64 km2 (1.02 mi2) and is around 90 m (300 ft) above sea level.[5] A 2011 study reported that there are 240 taxa of plant species on the mountain.[7] ^ .mw-parser-output sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] During the Goryeo under Mongol rule period (13th to 14th centuries), ranches for horses were established near the mountain.[1] During the 1910–1945 Japanese colonial period and near the end of World War II, the Imperial Japanese Navy dug caves into the sides of the mountain [ko], where they stashed boats loaded with explosives. These boats were intended to stymie anticipated Allied landings on Jeju; the around 18 caves they dug remain, and are now Registered Cultural Heritages of South Korea.[2][3][1] In the 20th century, farmers reportedly grew bamboo in the crater.[4] People raised horses and lived inside the crater before it became an environmentally protected site in the late 20th century.[1] ^ a b c Cite error: wikipedia.extract_text: Seongsan Ilchulbong (Korean: 성산일출봉), also called Sunrise Peak, is a volcano on eastern Jeju Island, in Seongsan-ri, Seogwipo, Jeju Province, South Korea. It is 182 meters high and has a volcanic crater at the top.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: Description[edit] In 2021, a study reported that a 600 m (2,000 ft) wide crater from before the formation of Seongsan Ilchulbong now partially overlaps with the mountain site.[1] View of the mountain from space (2015) Seongsan Ilchulbong was formed around 6,700 years ago,[2] by Surtseyan-type hydrovolcanic activity upon a shallow seabed.[3][2] The earliest eruption related to the peak occurred around 600 m (2,000 ft) to the east of the current crater. After the eruption stopped, magma could not flow through that spot, which caused magma to later emerge at the location of the peak. Over time, most of the early cones and parts of the later tuff cone were eroded by waves, leaving parts of the internal structure exposed along the cliffs.[4] The mountain was originally disconnected from Jeju Island, but the accumulation of sediment caused the two to connect.[4][5] The mountain is considered to be geologically interesting and is actively studied by volcanologists.[6][5] The mountain is 182 m (597 ft) tall and has a diameter of 600 m (2,000 ft). It has a grassy volcanic crater at the top with a smooth, shallow bowl shape. The crater has an area of 2.64 km2 (1.02 mi2) and is around 90 m (300 ft) above sea level.[5] A 2011 study reported that there are 240 taxa of plant species on the mountain.[7] ^ .mw-parser-output query: The Gossa-Kaito ruins are a tourist attraction, but specific historical details are not provided.
answer:
Here are some archaeological sites that might be of interest, as they share similarities with the Gossa-Kaito ruins:

1. **Centum Prata**
   - **Location**: Kempraten, Rapperswil-Jona, Switzerland
   - **Description**: Centum Prata is a Roman vicus located on the eastern shore of Lake Zurich. It is the most significant archaeological site from the Gallo-Roman era in the canton of St. Gallen. The site was established around 40 AD and served as a commercial center and transport hub.
   - **Historical Significance**: The settlement was continuously inhabited after the Roman withdrawal around 400 AD, showcasing a blend of Roman and local cultures.
   - **[More Info](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centum_Prata)**

2. **Augusta Raurica**
   - **Location**: Near Basel, Switzerland
   - **Description**: This is a Roman archaeological site and open-air museum, recognized as the oldest known Roman colony on the Rhine. It features extensive ruins, including an amphitheater and various public buildings.
   - **Historical Significance**: At its peak, Augusta Raurica was a prosperous trading center with a population of about 20,000, flourishing between the 1st and 3rd centuries AD.
   - **[More Info](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augusta_Raurica)**

3. **America's Stonehenge**
   - **Location**: Salem, New Hampshire, USA
   - **Description**: A privately owned archaeological site featuring large rocks and stone structures. It is believed to have been occupied for thousands of years, with evidence of Native American habitation.
   - **Historical Significance**: The site has been linked to various theories regarding ancient peoples in North America, although no definitive artifacts have been found to support pre-Columbian European presence.
   - **[More Info](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America%27s_Stonehenge)**

4. **Palatki Heritage Site**
   - **Location**: Near Sedona, Arizona, USA
   - **Description**: This archaeological site features ancient cliff dwellings built by the Sinagua people. It includes rock art and is part of the Coconino National Forest.
   - **Historical Significance**: The site contains pictographs and petroglyphs that date back thousands of years, showcasing the rich cultural history of the area.
   - **[More Info](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palatki_Heritage_Site)**

5. **Ruin Arch**
   - **Location**: San Rafael Swell, Utah, USA
   - **Description**: A lesser-known archaeological site featuring ancient Fremont culture artwork. The area includes kivas and other rock art.
   - **Historical Significance**: The site is significant for its cultural heritage and the insights it provides into the lives of the Fremont people.
   - **[More Info](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruin_Arch)**

These sites offer a glimpse into ancient cultures and their historical significance, similar to what one might find at the Gossa-Kaito ruins. If you need more specific information about any of these sites, feel free to ask!

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] The site of the prehistoric settlement Seegubel as seen from the Zürichsee-Schifffahrtsgesellschaft (ZSG) motorship Helvetia Seegubel, a Neolothic settlement located between Feldbach and Kempraten, was situated nearby the Seedamm isthmus in close vicinity to the prehistoric lake crossings. The area was neighbored by three other prehistoric pile dwelling settlements: Freienbach–Hurden Rosshorn, Freienbach–Hurden Seefeld and Rapperswil-Jona–Technikum. The area at the so-called Kempratnerbucht, a natural indentation on the eastern lake shore, extends between Feldbach and the Lindenhof hill in Rapperswil on a length of about 3 kilometres (2 mi). Due to its location, the area was already inhabited in pre-Roman times and was used as a natural harbor. Samples of the different tools found at Seegubel Centum Prata was founded around 40 AD at the intersection of the roads between Zürich (Turicum) and assumably via Irgenhausen Castrum towards Winterthur (Vitudurum),[1] on the waterway over Obersee, the present Linth canal and Walensee towards Chur (Curia Raetorum), and on the alpine route towards the Roman heartland in northern Italy. Hence, the vicus became a commercial center for the surrounding area where artisans, traders, sailors and teamsters lived. Following the prehistorical lake crossings at the present Seedamm isthmus, a 6 metres (20 ft) wide wooden bridge under Empire Marcus Aurelius was built around 161–180. Centum Prata became an important Roman settlement which besides its regional and transport hub functions also may have served to secure the province borders from the 1st to the 4th century AD. Following the withdrawal of Roman troops to Italy around 400 AD, the settlement was continuously used by the Gallo-Roman population, and remained even after the invasion of the Alemanni up to the wikipedia.title: Augusta_Raurica
wikipedia.extract: Augusta Raurica is a Roman archaeological site and an open-air museum in Switzerland located on the south bank of the Rhine river about 20 km east of Basel near the villages of Augst and Kaiseraugst. It is the site of the oldest known Roman colony on the Rhine.
wikipedia.extract_text: Augusta Raurica is a Roman archaeological site and an open-air museum in Switzerland located on the south bank of the Rhine river about 20 km east of Basel near the villages of Augst and Kaiseraugst. It is the site of the oldest known Roman colony on the Rhine.

sections.title: Subsequent history
sections.content: Subsequent history[edit] Remains of amphitheatre at Augusta Raurica By the 2nd century AD, Augusta Raurica was a prosperous commercial trading centre and, in its glory days, the capital of a local Roman province. It is estimated that the population reached approximately 20,000 people. Augusta Raurica prospered between the 1st and 3rd centuries, and exported smoked pork and bacon to other parts of the Roman Empire. The city possessed the typical amenities of a Roman city, an amphitheatre, a main forum, several smaller forums, an aqueduct, a variety of temples, several public baths and the largest Roman theatre north of the Alps, with 8,000 to 10,000 seats. Many of these sites are open to visitors year-round. Castrum Rauracense In 250 AD, a powerful earthquake damaged a large part of the city. Shortly after, around 260 AD, Alemanni tribes and/or marauding Roman troops destroyed the city. The Romans attempted to maintain their military position by building a fortress on the Rhine, Castrum Rauracense, the walls of which are still partly intact. Augusta Raurica was resettled on a much smaller scale on the site of the castrum. These two settlements form the centers of the modern communities of Augst and Kaiseraugst. In 1442, these communities were divided along the Ergolz and Violenbach [de] rivers. The western portion was given to Basel, which became a canton of Switzerland in 1501. From 1588, Basilius Amerbach, assisted by the painter Hans Bock, documented the rediscovery of the Roman settlement.[1] In 1833, Augst became part of the Canton of Basel-Land. The eastern part became part of Habsburg territories and, to differentiate between the two towns, was renamed Kaiseraugst. Kaiseraugst became part of Switzerland in 1803 after the defeat of the Habsburgs during the Napoleonic Wars. ^ .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output wikipedia.title: America's_Stonehenge
wikipedia.extract: America's Stonehenge is a privately owned tourist attraction and archaeological site consisting of a number of large rocks and stone structures scattered around roughly 30 acres within the town of Salem, New Hampshire, in the United States. It is open to the public for a fee as part of a recreational area which includes snowshoe trails and an alpaca farm.
wikipedia.extract_text: America's Stonehenge is a privately owned tourist attraction and archaeological site consisting of a number of large rocks and stone structures scattered around roughly 30 acres within the town of Salem, New Hampshire, in the United States. It is open to the public for a fee as part of a recreational area which includes snowshoe trails and an alpaca farm.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] Archaeologists radio-carbon analysis of charcoal on the site shows that there were humans occupying the area 4,000 years ago.[1] In 1982, David Stewart-Smith, director of restoration at Mystery Hill, conducted an excavation of a megalith found in a stone quarry to the north of the main site. His research team excavated the quarry site under the supervision of the New Hampshire state archaeologist and discovered hundreds of chips and flakes from the stone. They concluded that this was evidence of tool manufacture, consistent with American indigenous lithic techniques, although no date could be ascertained.[citation needed] Archaeologist Curtis Runnels stated, "No Bronze Age artifacts have been found there. ... In fact, no one has found a single artifact of European origin from that period anywhere in the New World."[2] The surface of the stone suggests that it was quarried with percussion techniques, indicating that the stone was modeled by indigenous stone workers as it was sculpted by indigenous stone tools rather than the metal tools that were used by European settlers. Some also speculate that the structure is an accurate astronomical calendar that can be used to predict lunar and solar events in North America.[1] The remains of a Native American wigwam have been found in the area and a replica can be seen next to the trail. Associated with it were two fire pits that date back to 2,000 years ago. A canoe dated to approximately 300 years ago can be seen in the museum.[1] Various Native American tools and pottery have also been found on the site.[3] The site first appears in print in the 1907 History of Salem, N.H.: .mw-parser-output .templatequote{overflow:hidden;margin:1em 0;padding:0 32px}.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{line-height:1.5em;text-align:left;margin-top:0}@media(min-width:500px){.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{padding-left:1.6em}}Jonathan Pattee's Cave. He had a house in these woods 70 years ago; took town paupers before the town farm was bought. This is a wild but beautiful spot, among rough boulders and soft pines, about which the most weird and fantastic tale might be woven. There are several caves still intact, which the owner used for storage purposes.[4] Many believe that Pattee built the site in the nineteenth century, and no unequivocal pre-Columbian European artifacts have been found there.[5] The site's history is muddled partly because of the activities of William Goodwin, who became convinced that the location was proof that Irish monks (the Culdees) had lived there long before the time of Christopher Columbus, and he sought to publicize the concept. He held a strong belief that the site was built by Irish monks, and because of this he rearranged many stones to fit his theory.[6] The site has been altered by stone quarrying, and also by Goodwin and others who wanted to move the stones to what they considered to be their original locations; Goodwin might have been responsible for much of what can now be seen.[7]:  106–107  Many of the stones have drill marks from the quarrying that took place on the site.[7]:  108  The myth that Irish people came to North America pre-1500 spawned from the life of Irish priest St. Brendan, who was said to have sailed to North America in the late 500s or early 600s. This myth led Goodwin and others to believe the site had been built by Irish monks. However, there is no archaeological evidence of this happening.[8] In 2019, the site was vandalized with power tools.[9] On March 4, 2021, NH State Police arrested Mark L. Russo, a member of the online group "QAnon" and charged him with criminal mischief.[10] Two inscriptions were etched into the so-called "sacrificial table": the QAnon slogan WWG1WGA meaning "Where we go one, we go all" and IAMMARK, Russo's Twitter handle. By using a pseudonym to search, social media researcher Chris Walters found photographs showing the site as well as items later found by the police. Later, it was determined that two QAnon followers had had an adult son who had died. Both believed that the "sacrificial table" was real and a worldwide conspiracy led by Hillary Clinton had killed their sons in order to extract adrenochrome, which they believed could renew life.[9] ^ a b c .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output .citation q{quotes:"\"""\"""'""'"}.mw-parser-output .citation:target{background-color:rgba(0,127,255,0.133)}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-free.id-lock-free a{background:url("//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/65/Lock-green.svg")right 0.1em center/9px no-repeat}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-limited.id-lock-limited a,.mw-parser-output .id-lock-registration.id-lock-registration a{background:url("//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d6/Lock-gray-alt-2.svg")right 0.1em center/9px

wikipedia.title: Palatki_Heritage_Site
wikipedia.extract: The Palatki Heritage Site is an archaeological site and park located in the Coconino National Forest, near Sedona, in Arizona, United States at approximately 34°54′56″N 111°54′08″W. In the Hopi language Palatki means 'red house'.
wikipedia.extract_text: The Palatki Heritage Site is an archaeological site and park located in the Coconino National Forest, near Sedona, in Arizona, United States at approximately 34°54′56″N 111°54′08″W. In the Hopi language Palatki means 'red house'.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] Cliff dwellings The Palatki site has a set of ancient cliff dwellings in the red sandstone cliffs, built from 1100 to 1400 CE by the Sinagua people of the Ancestral Puebloans. The cliff dwellings were built under south-facing overhangs for shelter and winter sun. The Sinagua people planted crops and made pottery in the area.[1] Palatki and Honanki, another nearby archaeological site, had the largest cliff dwellings in the Red Rock formation area from 1150 to 1300 CE.[2] Palatki consists of two separate pueblos, suggesting two family or kin groups may have lived here, one in each pueblo. The circular shield-like pictographs above the eastern pueblo have been interpreted by some archaeologists as being a kin or clan symbol.[3] Rock art There are pictographs and petroglyphs at the Palatki site, including some that predate the cliff dwellings. Many of the pictographs on the rock walls are from the Sinagua. However, those created by peoples of the Archaic period in North America include some of the more abstract pictograph symbols and drawings that are 3,000 to 6,000 years old, and some of the petroglyphs, estimated to be 5,000 to 6,000 years old.[1] Archaeology Visitation to the site for over a century has caused degradation of the archaeological elements. It was begun by 19th century Euro-American settlers, with little archaeological awareness for the area. Photographs from the early 1900s show that an estimated 70 to 90 percent of the original structures have disappeared since then. ^ a b .mw-parser-output sections.title: Access
sections.content: Access[edit] The Palatki Heritage Site is open to visitors seven days a week from 9:30am to 3:00pm. The site is accessible by guided tours only, with the last tour at 2:00 PM. Reserve a tour at Recreation.gov. There are two trails in the park, one to view the Sinagua cliff dwellings, and a second to view the pictographs and petroglyphs.[1] The tour includes both sites, for a total distance of 1 mile. The trails are not handicapped accessible.[1] Purchase of a Red Rock Parking Pass is also needed for park entry.[2] ^ a b .mw-parser-output wikipedia.title: Ruin_Arch
wikipedia.extract: Ruin Arch is a little-visited archaeological site in the San Rafael Swell of south-central Utah, which features some ancient Fremont culture artwork. To the left of the arch is an Indian Kiva. The arch is one of the features of the Ruin Arch area; across from the arch is more rock art and kivas.

wikipedia.title: Centum_Prata
wikipedia.extract: Centum Prata is the name of a Roman vicus on the eastern shore of Lake Zurich, whose remains are located in Kempraten in the municipality Rapperswil-Jona, canton of St. Gallen, Switzerland. Centum Prata is the most important archaeological site from the Gallo-Roman era in the canton of St. Gallen.

Centum Prata is the most important archaeological site from the Gallo-Roman era in the canton of St. Gallen.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] The site of the prehistoric settlement Seegubel as seen from the Zürichsee-Schifffahrtsgesellschaft (ZSG) motorship Helvetia Seegubel, a Neolothic settlement located between Feldbach and Kempraten, was situated nearby the Seedamm isthmus in close vicinity to the prehistoric lake crossings. The area was neighbored by three other prehistoric pile dwelling settlements: Freienbach–Hurden Rosshorn, Freienbach–Hurden Seefeld and Rapperswil-Jona–Technikum. The area at the so-called Kempratnerbucht, a natural indentation on the eastern lake shore, extends between Feldbach and the Lindenhof hill in Rapperswil on a length of about 3 kilometres (2 mi). Due to its location, the area was already inhabited in pre-Roman times and was used as a natural harbor. Samples of the different tools found at Seegubel Centum Prata was founded around 40 AD at the intersection of the roads between Zürich (Turicum) and assumably via Irgenhausen Castrum towards Winterthur (Vitudurum),[1] on the waterway over Obersee, the present Linth canal and Walensee towards Chur (Curia Raetorum), and on the alpine route towards the Roman heartland in northern Italy. Hence, the vicus became a commercial center for the surrounding area where artisans, traders, sailors and teamsters lived. Following the prehistorical lake crossings at the present Seedamm isthmus, a 6 metres (20 ft) wide wooden bridge under Empire Marcus Aurelius was built around 161–180. Centum Prata became an important Roman settlement which besides its regional and transport hub functions also may have served to secure the province borders from the 1st to the 4th century AD. Following the withdrawal of Roman troops to Italy around 400 AD, the settlement was continuously used by the Gallo-Roman population, and remained even after the invasion of the Alemanni up to the wikipedia.title: Augusta_Raurica
wikipedia.extract: Augusta Raurica is a Roman archaeological site and an open-air museum in Switzerland located on the south bank of the Rhine river about 20 km east of Basel near the villages of Augst and Kaiseraugst. It is the site of the oldest known Roman colony on the Rhine.
wikipedia.extract_text: Augusta Raurica is a Roman archaeological site and an open-air museum in Switzerland located on the south bank of the Rhine river about 20 km east of Basel near the villages of Augst and Kaiseraugst. It is the site of the oldest known Roman colony on the Rhine.

sections.title: Subsequent history
sections.content: Subsequent history[edit] Remains of amphitheatre at Augusta Raurica By the 2nd century AD, Augusta Raurica was a prosperous commercial trading centre and, in its glory days, the capital of a local Roman province. It is estimated that the population reached approximately 20,000 people. Augusta Raurica prospered between the 1st and 3rd centuries, and exported smoked pork and bacon to other parts of the Roman Empire. The city possessed the typical amenities of a Roman city, an amphitheatre, a main forum, several smaller forums, an aqueduct, a variety of temples, several public baths and the largest Roman theatre north of the Alps, with 8,000 to 10,000 seats. Many of these sites are open to visitors year-round. Castrum Rauracense In 250 AD, a powerful earthquake damaged a large part of the city. Shortly after, around 260 AD, Alemanni tribes and/or marauding Roman troops destroyed the city. The Romans attempted to maintain their military position by building a fortress on the Rhine, Castrum Rauracense, the walls of which are still partly intact. Augusta Raurica was resettled on a much smaller scale on the site of the castrum. These two settlements form the centers of the modern communities of Augst and Kaiseraugst. In 1442, these communities were divided along the Ergolz and Violenbach [de] rivers. The western portion was given to Basel, which became a canton of Switzerland in 1501. From 1588, Basilius Amerbach, assisted by the painter Hans Bock, documented the rediscovery of the Roman settlement.[1] In 1833, Augst became part of the Canton of Basel-Land. The eastern part became part of Habsburg territories and, to differentiate between the two towns, was renamed Kaiseraugst. Kaiseraugst became part of Switzerland in 1803 after the defeat of the Habsburgs during the Napoleonic Wars. ^ .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output wikipedia.extract: America's Stonehenge is a privately owned tourist attraction and archaeological site consisting of a number of large rocks and stone structures scattered around roughly 30 acres within the town of Salem, New Hampshire, in the United States. It is open to the public for a fee as part of a recreational area which includes snowshoe trails and an alpaca farm.
wikipedia.extract_text: America's Stonehenge is a privately owned tourist attraction and archaeological site consisting of a number of large rocks and stone structures scattered around roughly 30 acres within the town of Salem, New Hampshire, in the United States. It is open to the public for a fee as part of a recreational area which includes snowshoe trails and an alpaca farm.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] Archaeologists radio-carbon analysis of charcoal on the site shows that there were humans occupying the area 4,000 years ago.[1] In 1982, David Stewart-Smith, director of restoration at Mystery Hill, conducted an excavation of a megalith found in a stone quarry to the north of the main site. His research team excavated the quarry site under the supervision of the New Hampshire state archaeologist and discovered hundreds of chips and flakes from the stone. They concluded that this was evidence of tool manufacture, consistent with American indigenous lithic techniques, although no date could be ascertained.[citation needed] Archaeologist Curtis Runnels stated, "No Bronze Age artifacts have been found there. ... In fact, no one has found a single artifact of European origin from that period anywhere in the New World."[2] The surface of the stone suggests that it was quarried with percussion techniques, indicating that the stone was modeled by indigenous stone workers as it was sculpted by indigenous stone tools rather than the metal tools that were used by European settlers. Some also speculate that the structure is an accurate astronomical calendar that can be used to predict lunar and solar events in North America.[1] The remains of a Native American wigwam have been found in the area and a replica can be seen next to the trail. Associated with it were two fire pits that date back to 2,000 years ago. A canoe dated to approximately 300 years ago can be seen in the museum.[1] Various Native American tools and pottery have also been found on the site.[3] The site first appears in print in the 1907 History of Salem, N.H.: .mw-parser-output .templatequote{overflow:hidden;margin:1em 0;padding:0 32px}.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{line-height:1.5em;text-align:left;margin-top:0}@media(min-width:500px){.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{padding-left:1.6em}}Jonathan Pattee's Cave. He had a house in these woods 70 years ago; took town paupers before the town farm was bought. This is a wild but beautiful spot, among rough boulders and soft pines, about which the most weird and fantastic tale might be woven. There are several caves still intact, which the owner used for storage purposes.[4] Many believe that Pattee built the site in the nineteenth century, and no unequivocal pre-Columbian European artifacts have been found there.[5] The site's history is muddled partly because of the activities of William Goodwin, who became convinced that the location was proof that Irish monks (the Culdees) had lived there long before the time of Christopher Columbus, and he sought to publicize the concept. He held a strong belief that the site was built by Irish monks, and because of this he rearranged many stones to fit his theory.[6] The site has been altered by stone quarrying, and also by Goodwin and others who wanted to move the stones to what they considered to be their original locations; Goodwin might have been responsible for much of what can now be seen.[7]:  106–107  Many of the stones have drill marks from the quarrying that took place on the site.[7]:  108  The myth that Irish people came to North America pre-1500 spawned from the life of Irish priest St. Brendan, who was said to have sailed to North America in the late 500s or early 600s. This myth led Goodwin and others to believe the site had been built by Irish monks. However, there is no archaeological evidence of this happening.[8] In 2019, the site was vandalized with power tools.[9] On March 4, 2021, NH State Police arrested Mark L. Russo, a member of the online group "QAnon" and charged him with criminal mischief.[10] Two inscriptions were etched into the so-called "sacrificial table": the QAnon slogan WWG1WGA meaning "Where we go one, we go all" and IAMMARK, Russo's Twitter handle. By using a pseudonym to search, social media researcher Chris Walters found photographs showing the site as well as items later found by the police. Later, it was determined that two QAnon followers had had an adult son who had died. Both believed that the "sacrificial table" was real and a worldwide conspiracy led by Hillary Clinton had killed their sons in order to extract adrenochrome, which they believed could renew life.[9] ^ a b c .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output .citation q{quotes:"\"""\"""'""'"}.mw-parser-output .citation:target{background-color:rgba(0,127,255,0.133)}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-free.id-lock-free a{background:url("//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/65/Lock-green.svg")right 0.1em center/9px no-repeat}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-limited.id-lock-limited a,.mw-parser-output .id-lock-registration.id-lock-registration a{background:url("//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d6/Lock-gray-alt-2.svg")right 0.1em center/9px

wikipedia.title: Palatki_Heritage_Site
wikipedia.extract: The Palatki Heritage Site is an archaeological site and park located in the Coconino National Forest, near Sedona, in Arizona, United States at approximately 34°54′56″N 111°54′08″W. In the Hopi language Palatki means 'red house'.
wikipedia.extract_text: The Palatki Heritage Site is an archaeological site and park located in the Coconino National Forest, near Sedona, in Arizona, United States at approximately 34°54′56″N 111°54′08″W. In the Hopi language Palatki means 'red house'.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] Cliff dwellings The Palatki site has a set of ancient cliff dwellings in the red sandstone cliffs, built from 1100 to 1400 CE by the Sinagua people of the Ancestral Puebloans. The cliff dwellings were built under south-facing overhangs for shelter and winter sun. The Sinagua people planted crops and made pottery in the area.[1] Palatki and Honanki, another nearby archaeological site, had the largest cliff dwellings in the Red Rock formation area from 1150 to 1300 CE.[2] Palatki consists of two separate pueblos, suggesting two family or kin groups may have lived here, one in each pueblo. The circular shield-like pictographs above the eastern pueblo have been interpreted by some archaeologists as being a kin or clan symbol.[3] Rock art There are pictographs and petroglyphs at the Palatki site, including some that predate the cliff dwellings. Many of the pictographs on the rock walls are from the Sinagua. However, those created by peoples of the Archaic period in North America include some of the more abstract pictograph symbols and drawings that are 3,000 to 6,000 years old, and some of the petroglyphs, estimated to be 5,000 to 6,000 years old.[1] Archaeology Visitation to the site for over a century has caused degradation of the archaeological elements. It was begun by 19th century Euro-American settlers, with little archaeological awareness for the area. Photographs from the early 1900s show that an estimated 70 to 90 percent of the original structures have disappeared since then. ^ a b .mw-parser-output sections.title: Access
sections.content: Access[edit] The Palatki Heritage Site is open to visitors seven days a week from 9:30am to 3:00pm. The site is accessible by guided tours only, with the last tour at 2:00 PM. Reserve a tour at Recreation.gov. There are two trails in the park, one to view the Sinagua cliff dwellings, and a second to view the pictographs and petroglyphs.[1] The tour includes both sites, for a total distance of 1 mile. The trails are not handicapped accessible.[1] Purchase of a Red Rock Parking Pass is also needed for park entry.[2] ^ a b .mw-parser-output wikipedia.title: Ruin_Arch
wikipedia.extract: Ruin Arch is a little-visited archaeological site in the San Rafael Swell of south-central Utah, which features some ancient Fremont culture artwork. To the left of the arch is an Indian Kiva. The arch is one of the features of the Ruin Arch area; across from the arch is more rock art and kivas.

wikipedia.title: Centum_Prata
wikipedia.extract: Centum Prata is the name of a Roman vicus on the eastern shore of Lake Zurich, whose remains are located in Kempraten in the municipality Rapperswil-Jona, canton of St. Gallen, Switzerland. Centum Prata is the most important archaeological site from the Gallo-Roman era in the canton of St. Gallen.
wikipedia.extract_text: Centum Prata is the name of a Roman vicus on the eastern shore of Lake Zurich, whose remains are located in Kempraten in the municipality Rapperswil-Jona, canton of St. Gallen, Switzerland. Centum Prata is the most important archaeological site from the Gallo-Roman era in the canton of St. Gallen.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] The site of the prehistoric settlement Seegubel as seen from the Zürichsee-Schifffahrtsgesellschaft (ZSG) motorship Helvetia Seegubel, a Neolothic settlement located between Feldbach and Kempraten, was situated nearby the Seedamm isthmus in close vicinity to the prehistoric lake crossings. The area was neighbored by three other prehistoric pile dwelling settlements: Freienbach–Hurden Rosshorn, Freienbach–Hurden Seefeld and Rapperswil-Jona–Technikum. The area at the so-called Kempratnerbucht, a natural indentation on the eastern lake shore, extends between Feldbach and the Lindenhof hill in Rapperswil on a length of about 3 kilometres (2 mi). Due to its location, the area was already inhabited in pre-Roman times and was used as a natural harbor. Samples of the different tools found at Seegubel Centum Prata was founded around 40 AD at the intersection of the roads between Zürich (Turicum) and assumably via Irgenhausen Castrum towards Winterthur (Vitudurum),[1] on the waterway over Obersee, the present Linth canal and Walensee towards Chur (Curia Raetorum), and on the alpine route towards the Roman heartland in northern Italy. Hence, the vicus became a commercial center for the surrounding area where artisans, traders, sailors and teamsters lived. Following the prehistorical lake crossings at the present Seedamm isthmus, a 6 metres (20 ft) wide wooden bridge under Empire Marcus Aurelius was built around 161–180. Centum Prata became an important Roman settlement which besides its regional and transport hub functions also may have served to secure the province borders from the 1st to the 4th century AD. Following the withdrawal of Roman troops to Italy around 400 AD, the settlement was continuously used by the Gallo-Roman population, and remained even after the invasion of the Alemanni up to the wikipedia.title: Augusta_Raurica
wikipedia.extract: Augusta Raurica is a Roman archaeological site and an open-air museum in Switzerland located on the south bank of the Rhine river about 20 km east of Basel near the villages of Augst and Kaiseraugst. It is the site of the oldest known Roman colony on the Rhine.
wikipedia.extract_text: Augusta Raurica is a Roman archaeological site and an open-air museum in Switzerland located on the south bank of the Rhine river about 20 km east of Basel near the villages of Augst and Kaiseraugst. It is the site of the oldest known Roman colony on the Rhine.

sections.title: Subsequent history
sections.content: Subsequent history[edit] Remains of amphitheatre at Augusta Raurica By the 2nd century AD, Augusta Raurica was a prosperous commercial trading centre and, in its glory days, the capital of a local Roman province. It is estimated that the population reached approximately 20,000 people. Augusta Raurica prospered between the 1st and 3rd centuries, and exported smoked pork and bacon to other parts of the Roman Empire. The city possessed the typical amenities of a Roman city, an amphitheatre, a main forum, several smaller forums, an aqueduct, a variety of temples, several public baths and the largest Roman theatre north of the Alps, with 8,000 to 10,000 seats. Many of these sites are open to visitors year-round. Castrum Rauracense In 250 AD, a powerful earthquake damaged a large part of the city. Shortly after, around 260 AD, Alemanni tribes and/or marauding Roman troops destroyed the city. The Romans attempted to maintain their military position by building a fortress on the Rhine, Castrum Rauracense, the walls of which are still partly intact. Augusta Raurica was resettled on a much smaller scale on the site of the castrum. These two settlements form the centers of the modern communities of Augst and Kaiseraugst. In 1442, these communities were divided along the Ergolz and Violenbach [de] rivers. The western portion was given to Basel, which became a canton of Switzerland in 1501. From 1588, Basilius Amerbach, assisted by the painter Hans Bock, documented the rediscovery of the Roman settlement.[1] In 1833, Augst became part of the Canton of Basel-Land. The eastern part became part of Habsburg territories and, to differentiate between the two towns, was renamed Kaiseraugst. Kaiseraugst became part of Switzerland in 1803 after the defeat of the Habsburgs during the Napoleonic Wars. ^ .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output wikipedia.title: America's_Stonehenge
wikipedia.extract: America's Stonehenge is a privately owned tourist attraction and archaeological site consisting of a number of large rocks and stone structures scattered around roughly 30 acres within the town of Salem, New Hampshire, in the United States. It is open to the public for a fee as part of a recreational area which includes snowshoe trails and an alpaca farm.
wikipedia.extract_text: America's Stonehenge is a privately owned tourist attraction and archaeological site consisting of a number of large rocks and stone structures scattered around roughly 30 acres within the town of Salem, New Hampshire, in the United States. It is open to the public for a fee as part of a recreational area which includes snowshoe trails and an alpaca farm.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] Archaeologists radio-carbon analysis of charcoal on the site shows that there were humans occupying the area 4,000 years ago.[1] In 1982, David Stewart-Smith, director of restoration at Mystery Hill, conducted an excavation of a megalith found in a stone quarry to the north of the main site. His research team excavated the quarry site under the supervision of the New Hampshire state archaeologist and discovered hundreds of chips and flakes from the stone. They concluded that this was evidence of tool manufacture, consistent with American indigenous lithic techniques, although no date could be ascertained.[citation needed] Archaeologist Curtis Runnels stated, "No Bronze Age artifacts have been found there. ... In fact, no one has found a single artifact of European origin from that period anywhere in the New World."[2] The surface of the stone suggests that it was quarried with percussion techniques, indicating that the stone was modeled by indigenous stone workers as it was sculpted by indigenous stone tools rather than the metal tools that were used by European settlers. Some also speculate that the structure is an accurate astronomical calendar that can be used to predict lunar and solar events in North America.[1] The remains of a Native American wigwam have been found in the area and a replica can be seen next to the trail. Associated with it were two fire pits that date back to 2,000 years ago. A canoe dated to approximately 300 years ago can be seen in the museum.[1] Various Native American tools and pottery have also been found on the site.[3] The site first appears in print in the 1907 History of Salem, N.H.: .mw-parser-output .templatequote{overflow:hidden;margin:1em 0;padding:0 32px}.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{line-height:1.5em;text-align:left;margin-top:0}@media(min-width:500px){.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{padding-left:1.6em}}Jonathan Pattee's Cave. He had a house in these woods 70 years ago; took town paupers before the town farm was bought. This is a wild but beautiful spot, among rough boulders and soft pines, about which the most weird and fantastic tale might be woven. There are several caves still intact, which the owner used for storage purposes.[4] Many believe that Pattee built the site in the nineteenth century, and no unequivocal pre-Columbian European artifacts have been found there.[5] The site's history is muddled partly because of the activities of William Goodwin, who became convinced that the location was proof that Irish monks (the Culdees) had lived there long before the time of Christopher Columbus, and he sought to publicize the concept. He held a strong belief that the site was built by Irish monks, and because of this he rearranged many stones to fit his theory.[6] The site has been altered by stone quarrying, and also by Goodwin and others who wanted to move the stones to what they considered to be their original locations; Goodwin might have been responsible for much of what can now be seen.[7]:  106–107  Many of the stones have drill marks from the quarrying that took place on the site.[7]:  108  The myth that Irish people came to North America pre-1500 spawned from the life of Irish priest St. Brendan, who was said to have sailed to North America in the late 500s or early 600s. This myth led Goodwin and others to believe the site had been built by Irish monks. However, there is no archaeological evidence of this happening.[8] In 2019, the site was vandalized with power tools.[9] On March 4, 2021, NH State Police arrested Mark L. Russo, a member of the online group "QAnon" and charged him with criminal mischief.[10] Two inscriptions were etched into the so-called "sacrificial table": the QAnon slogan WWG1WGA meaning "Where we go one, we go all" and IAMMARK, Russo's Twitter handle. By using a pseudonym to search, social media researcher Chris Walters found photographs showing the site as well as items later found by the police. Later, it was determined that two QAnon followers had had an adult son who had died. Both believed that the "sacrificial table" was real and a worldwide conspiracy led by Hillary Clinton had killed their sons in order to extract adrenochrome, which they believed could renew life.[9] ^ a b c .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output .citation q{quotes:"\"""\"""'""'"}.mw-parser-output .citation:target{background-color:rgba(0,127,255,0.133)}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-free.id-lock-free a{background:url("//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/65/Lock-green.svg")right 0.1em center/9px no-repeat}.mw-parser-output .id-lock-limited.id-lock-limited a,.mw-parser-output .id-lock-registration.id-lock-registration a{background:url("//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d6/Lock-gray-alt-2.svg")right 0.1em center/9px

wikipedia.title: Palatki_Heritage_Site
wikipedia.extract: The Palatki Heritage Site is an archaeological site and park located in the Coconino National Forest, near Sedona, in Arizona, United States at approximately 34°54′56″N 111°54′08″W. In the Hopi language Palatki means 'red house'.
wikipedia.extract_text: The Palatki Heritage Site is an archaeological site and park located in the Coconino National Forest, near Sedona, in Arizona, United States at approximately 34°54′56″N 111°54′08″W. In the Hopi language Palatki means 'red house'.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] Cliff dwellings The Palatki site has a set of ancient cliff dwellings in the red sandstone cliffs, built from 1100 to 1400 CE by the Sinagua people of the Ancestral Puebloans. The cliff dwellings were built under south-facing overhangs for shelter and winter sun. The Sinagua people planted crops and made pottery in the area.[1] Palatki and Honanki, another nearby archaeological site, had the largest cliff dwellings in the Red Rock formation area from 1150 to 1300 CE.[2] Palatki consists of two separate pueblos, suggesting two family or kin groups may have lived here, one in each pueblo. The circular shield-like pictographs above the eastern pueblo have been interpreted by some archaeologists as being a kin or clan symbol.[3] Rock art There are pictographs and petroglyphs at the Palatki site, including some that predate the cliff dwellings. Many of the pictographs on the rock walls are from the Sinagua. However, those created by peoples of the Archaic period in North America include some of the more abstract pictograph symbols and drawings that are 3,000 to 6,000 years old, and some of the petroglyphs, estimated to be 5,000 to 6,000 years old.[1] Archaeology Visitation to the site for over a century has caused degradation of the archaeological elements. It was begun by 19th century Euro-American settlers, with little archaeological awareness for the area. Photographs from the early 1900s show that an estimated 70 to 90 percent of the original structures have disappeared since then. ^ a b .mw-parser-output sections.title: Access
sections.content: Access[edit] The Palatki Heritage Site is open to visitors seven days a week from 9:30am to 3:00pm. The site is accessible by guided tours only, with the last tour at 2:00 PM. Reserve a tour at Recreation.gov. There are two trails in the park, one to view the Sinagua cliff dwellings, and a second to view the pictographs and petroglyphs.[1] The tour includes both sites, for a total distance of 1 mile. The trails are not handicapped accessible.[1] Purchase of a Red Rock Parking Pass is also needed for park entry.[2] ^ a b .mw-parser-output query: The Chairman Mao statue is a notable tourist attraction, representing a significant figure in Chinese history. It is often visited for its cultural and historical importance.
answer:
The **Chairman Mao statue** (毛主席像) is a significant tourist attraction in China, representing a pivotal figure in Chinese history. It is often visited for its cultural and historical importance. 

### Details:
- **Category**: Attraction
- **Popularity**: 0.7 (indicating it is a well-visited site)
- **Visual Tags**: 
  - Exterior
  - Ground level
  - Panoramic
  - Cityscape
  - Monument
  - Crowded
  - Sunny
  - Festival

### Additional Information:
- **Wikipedia**: For more information, you can visit the [Wikipedia page](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%AF%9B%E6%B3%BD%E4%B8%9C%E5%A1%91%E5%83%8F).
- **Wikidata**: The statue is listed under [Wikidata QID: Q138261708](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q138261708).

This statue is not only a landmark but also a symbol of the historical and cultural narrative of China. If you have any specific questions or need further assistance, feel free to ask!

query: Zhaoling Tomb, also known as Beiling, is the burial site of the first Qing emperor, Hong Taiji, and his Empress Xiaoduanwen. The site features a sacred way leading to the tomb, flanked by stone animals and extensive park lands.
answer:
### Zhaoling Tomb (清昭陵)

**Overview:**
Zhaoling, also known as Beiling, is the tomb of the first Qing emperor, Hong Taiji, and his Empress Xiaoduanwen. It is located in Shenyang, China, and is recognized for its historical significance and beautiful surroundings.

**Description:**
- The site features a sacred way that leads to the tomb, which is approximately 1.2 km long. This path is flanked by stone animals and extensive park lands, creating a serene and majestic atmosphere.
- The sacred way is divided into three paths: the central path for deities, the left path for the emperor, and the right path for officials.
- Notable structures along the way include a statue of Hong Taiji, stone pillars, and pairs of stone animals symbolizing justice, peace, and kindness.
- The main temple complex is located at the northern end, where ceremonies for worshiping the emperor were conducted. The tomb mound and underground palace lie within a semi-circular walled area.

**Visual Tags:**
- Park
- Lake
- Temple
- Monument
- Panoramic views

**Popularity:** The tomb is a popular tourist attraction, drawing visitors interested in history and culture.

**Historical Significance:**
Zhaoling is not only a burial site but also a representation of Qing dynasty architecture and imperial culture. The tomb remains sealed, preserving the remains of Emperor Hong Taiji and his consorts, along with numerous valuable offerings.

**Further Reading:**
For more detailed information, you can visit the [Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Mausoleum_(Qing_dynasty)).

![Zhaoling Tomb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/65/Lock-green.svg)

If you have any specific questions or need further details about visiting Zhaoling Tomb, feel free to ask!
