sections.title: Description
sections.content: Description[edit] The site is aligned on a north–south axis set west of Shenyang city's old north axis. This access forms the sacred way of about 1.2 km that leads from the park gate to the tomb buildings. The way itself is made in three paths. The centre path was for the deities only or bearers of offerings. The path of the lefthand (west) of the sacred way was for the ruling emperor and the righthand (east) path was for officials and imperial staff. Halfway along the royal way stands a statue of Hong Taiji in a bold stance and wearing military dress. To either side lie extensive park lands of forest and lakes. At the northern end of the royal way, the route crosses a bridge over a lake beyond which stand a series of gates that mark the entrance to the inner tomb area.[1] The first gate is made of marble with ornate carvings. Heavy steel supports have been added to the front and back of this gate to prevent it falling over. The second gate takes you through the walls that surround the tomb. The royal way continues through forested land. A pair of stone pillars mark the beginning of the inner tomb structures. To either side of the route stand four pairs of stone animals. These are two xiezhi (mythical beasts that could tell good from evil. Here they represent the justice of the Emperor), two qilin (representing peace and kindness), two white horses, and lastly two camels. Beyond these guardians, the way is blocked by a small building inside which is a large stele. This stele tells of the deeds done by the dead emperor. It is mounted on top of a large statue of a turtle. After this, to either side of the way stand four buildings. These were used by the emperor and his staff to prepare themselves and their offerings before their ceremony to honor the past emperor.[1] Three stations of Shenyang Metro Line 2 serve this area: Beiling Gongyuan Station, Lingxi Station, and Xinle Yizhi Station. Main temple complex[edit] After these stands the main temple complex. This is a walled area within which the ceremonies for worshiping the emperor were carried out. The tomb mound and underground palace stand in a semi-circular walled area north of the temple area. The temple walls are high, with a walkway set on top of them. Each corner is marked with a small tower and two larger towers stand over the north and south gates of the temple area. Within the temple complex's walls stand five buildings. The first four, set on either side of the central axis, were used for preparing the ceremony. At the northern end of the temple area, on top of the central axis, stands the altar building. It was here that the rites of worship were carried out. The building houses representations of the dead emperor. In front of the altar building, the emperor and his household would make offerings to their ancestors. To the south west of the altar stands a small stone structure in which offerings, after being presented on the altar, would be burnt. Beyond the altar building, a final gate leads out of the temple area to the wall of the tomb mound itself. The underground tomb remains sealed, its contents hidden from view. sections.title: Description
sections.content: Description[edit] The site is aligned on a north–south axis set west of Shenyang city's old north axis. This access forms the sacred way of about 1.2 km that leads from the park gate to the tomb buildings. The way itself is made in three paths. The centre path was for the deities only or bearers of offerings. The path of the lefthand (west) of the sacred way was for the ruling emperor and the righthand (east) path was for officials and imperial staff. Halfway along the royal way stands a statue of Hong Taiji in a bold stance and wearing military dress. To either side lie extensive park lands of forest and lakes. At the northern end of the royal way, the route crosses a bridge over a lake beyond which stand a series of gates that mark the entrance to the inner tomb area.[1] The first gate is made of marble with ornate carvings. Heavy steel supports have been added to the front and back of this gate to prevent it falling over. The second gate takes you through the walls that surround the tomb. The royal way continues through forested land. A pair of stone pillars mark the beginning of the inner tomb structures. To either side of the route stand four pairs of stone animals. These are two xiezhi (mythical beasts that could tell good from evil. Here they represent the justice of the Emperor), two qilin (representing peace and kindness), two white horses, and lastly two camels. Beyond these guardians, the way is blocked by a small building inside which is a large stele. This stele tells of the deeds done by the dead emperor. It is mounted on top of a large statue of a turtle. After this, to either side of the way stand four buildings. These were used by the emperor and his staff to prepare themselves and their offerings before their ceremony to honor the past emperor.[1] Three stations of Shenyang Metro Line 2 serve this area: Beiling Gongyuan Station, Lingxi Station, and Xinle Yizhi Station. Main temple complex[edit] After these stands the main temple complex. This is a walled area within which the ceremonies for worshiping the emperor were carried out. The tomb mound and underground palace stand in a semi-circular walled area north of the temple area. The temple walls are high, with a walkway set on top of them. Each corner is marked with a small tower and two larger towers stand over the north and south gates of the temple area. Within the temple complex's walls stand five buildings. The first four, set on either side of the central axis, were used for preparing the ceremony. At the northern end of the temple area, on top of the central axis, stands the altar building. It was here that the rites of worship were carried out. The building houses representations of the dead emperor. In front of the altar building, the emperor and his household would make offerings to their ancestors. To the south west of the altar stands a small stone structure in which offerings, after being presented on the altar, would be burnt. Beyond the altar building, a final gate leads out of the temple area to the wall of the tomb mound itself. The underground tomb remains sealed, its contents hidden from view. wikipedia.extract: Zhaoling, also known as Beiling is the tomb of the first Qing emperor, Hong Taiji, and his Empress Xiaoduanwen.
wikipedia.extract_text: Zhaoling, also known as Beiling is the tomb of the first Qing emperor, Hong Taiji, and his Empress Xiaoduanwen.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: Description[edit] The site is aligned on a north–south axis set west of Shenyang city's old north axis. This access forms the sacred way of about 1.2 km that leads from the park gate to the tomb buildings. The way itself is made in three paths. The centre path was for the deities only or bearers of offerings. The path of the lefthand (west) of the sacred way was for the ruling emperor and the righthand (east) path was for officials and imperial staff. Halfway along the royal way stands a statue of Hong Taiji in a bold stance and wearing military dress. To either side lie extensive park lands of forest and lakes. At the northern end of the royal way, the route crosses a bridge over a lake beyond which stand a series of gates that mark the entrance to the inner tomb area.[1] The first gate is made of marble with ornate carvings. Heavy steel supports have been added to the front and back of this gate to prevent it falling over. The second gate takes you through the walls that surround the tomb. The royal way continues through forested land. A pair of stone pillars mark the beginning of the inner tomb structures. To either side of the route stand four pairs of stone animals. These are two xiezhi (mythical beasts that could tell good from evil. Here they represent the justice of the Emperor), two qilin (representing peace and kindness), two white horses, and lastly two camels. Beyond these guardians, the way is blocked by a small building inside which is a large stele. This stele tells of the deeds done by the dead emperor. It is mounted on top of a large statue of a turtle. After this, to either side of the way stand four buildings. These were used by the emperor and his staff to prepare themselves and their offerings before their ceremony to honor the past emperor.[1] Three stations of Shenyang Metro Line 2 serve this area: Beiling Gongyuan Station, Lingxi Station, and Xinle Yizhi Station. Main temple complex[edit] After these stands the main temple complex. This is a walled area within which the ceremonies for worshiping the emperor were carried out. The tomb mound and underground palace stand in a semi-circular walled area north of the temple area. The temple walls are high, with a walkway set on top of them. Each corner is marked with a small tower and two larger towers stand over the north and south gates of the temple area. Within the temple complex's walls stand five buildings. The first four, set on either side of the central axis, were used for preparing the ceremony. At the northern end of the temple area, on top of the central axis, stands the altar building. It was here that the rites of worship were carried out. The building houses representations of the dead emperor. In front of the altar building, the emperor and his household would make offerings to their ancestors. To the south west of the altar stands a small stone structure in which offerings, after being presented on the altar, would be burnt. Beyond the altar building, a final gate leads out of the temple area to the wall of the tomb mound itself. The underground tomb remains sealed, its contents hidden from view. The tomb mound and underground palace stand in a semi-circular walled area north of the temple area. The temple walls are high, with a walkway set on top of them. Each corner is marked with a small tower and two larger towers stand over the north and south gates of the temple area. Within the temple complex's walls stand five buildings. The first four, set on either side of the central axis, were used for preparing the ceremony. At the northern end of the temple area, on top of the central axis, stands the altar building. query: Lingyin Temple, founded in 328 AD, is a significant Chan Buddhist temple near Hangzhou, known for its pagodas and grottos. It has been rebuilt multiple times and is regarded as one of the wealthiest monasteries in China, attracting both pilgrims and tourists.
answer:
**Lingyin Temple (灵隐寺)** is a prominent Chan Buddhist temple located near Hangzhou, China. Founded in **328 AD**, it is renowned for its beautiful pagodas and grottos. The temple's name translates to "Temple of the Soul's Retreat" in English.

### Key Information:
- **Category**: Attraction
- **Popularity**: Moderate (0.7)
- **Historical Significance**: 
  - The temple has a rich history, having been a significant monastery in the Jiangnan region since its inception. 
  - It was founded by an Indian monk named Huili during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
  - At its peak under the Wuyue Kingdom, it featured 18 pavilions and over 1300 dormitory rooms for monks.
  - The temple has been rebuilt multiple times, with significant restorations occurring during the late Qing dynasty and after the Cultural Revolution.

### Notable Features:
- **Architecture**: The temple complex includes various halls and pavilions, showcasing traditional Chinese architectural styles.
- **Surroundings**: The temple is set against a backdrop of mountains, enhancing its scenic beauty.
- **Cultural Importance**: It attracts both pilgrims and tourists, making it one of the wealthiest monasteries in China.

### Additional Resources:
- For more detailed historical context, you can visit the [Wikipedia page on Lingyin Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingyin_Temple).

### Visual Tags:
The temple is associated with various visual tags, including:
- Temple

- Seasonal greenery

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] According to tradition, the monastery was founded in 328 AD during the Eastern Jin dynasty (266–420) by an Indian monk, named Huili in Chinese. From its inception, Lingyin was a famous monastery in the Jiangnan region.[1] At its peak under the Wuyue Kingdom (907–978), the temple boasted 18 pavilions, 72 halls, more than 1300 dormitory rooms, inhabited by more than 3000 monks. Many of the rich Buddhist carvings in the Feilai Feng grottos and surrounding mountains also date from this era. During the Southern Song (1127–1279), the monastery was regarded as one of the ten most important temples of the Chan sect in the Jiangnan region. However, its prominence has not saved the temple from marauders. It has been rebuilt no less than sixteen times since then. While certain existing buildings date from previous Chinese dynasties, much of the current buildings are modern restorations from the late Qing (1644–1911) period. Over the course of the Cultural Revolution, the temple and grounds suffered damage from Hangzhou's Red Guards but the planned destruction of the temple in 1966 was successfully stopped by locals and students from Zhejiang University, who had been shocked and galvanized by the Guards' ransacking of the patriotic general Yue Fei's tomb.[2] Subsequently, the temple was offered a measure of protection by direct instructions from Premier Zhou Enlai. Today the temple is thriving as a destination for both pilgrims and tourists. It is regarded as one of the wealthiest monasteries in China, and regular pilgrims have included former paramount leader Deng Xiaoping. ^ Zi (2012), p. 85. ^ He (2006).

It is regarded as one of the wealthiest monasteries in China, and regular pilgrims have included former paramount leader Deng Xiaoping. ^ Zi (2012), p. 85. ^ He (2006).

query: Mawsynram is a town in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya, India, known for receiving the highest rainfall in the country and reportedly the wettest place on Earth. It has set multiple records for rainfall, including a significant amount in a single day.
answer:
### Mawsynram: The Wettest Place on Earth

**Location:**  
Mawsynram is a town located in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya, India, approximately 69 km (43 miles) from Shillong, the state capital.

**Rainfall Records:**  
Mawsynram is renowned for receiving the highest average annual rainfall in India, estimated at **11,872 millimeters (467.4 inches)**. It has set several records for rainfall, including a staggering **26,000 millimeters (1,023.6 inches)** in 1985, according to the Guinness Book of World Records. Most recently, on **June 17, 2022**, it recorded **1,003.2 millimeters (39.50 inches)** of rain in just 24 hours, marking its highest single-day rainfall.

**Climate:**  
The town experiences a subtropical highland climate characterized by a long monsoonal season and a brief dry season. The majority of its rainfall occurs during the monsoon months, with average annual precipitation exceeding **10,000 millimeters (390 inches)**.

**Natural Landmarks:**  
Mawsynram is also home to natural attractions, including the **Mawjymbuin Cave**, famous for its unique stalagmites and stalactites.

**Visual Tags:**  
The area is depicted with tags such as **cloudy**, **rainy**, **mountain**, and **valley**, reflecting its lush and wet environment.

**Further Reading:**  
For more detailed information, you can visit the [Wikipedia page on Mawsynram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mawsynram).

![Mawsynram](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/65/Lock-green.svg)

### Summary
Mawsynram is not only a remarkable destination for its climatic records but also offers stunning natural beauty and unique geological features, making it a must-visit for those interested in experiencing one of the world's most extraordinary weather phenomena.

wikipedia.extract:
Mawsynram is a town in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya state in Northeastern India, 69 km (43 mi) from Shillong, the state capital. Mawsynram receives the highest rainfall in India. It is reportedly the wettest place on Earth, with an average annual rainfall of 11,872 millimetres (467.4 in). According to the Guinness Book of World Records, Mawsynram received 26,000 millimetres (1,023.6 in) of rainfall in 1985.
Mawsynram received 745.3 millimetres (29.34 in) of rainfall on 19 August 2015. On 17 June 2022, Mawsynram set a new record by receiving 1,003.2 millimetres (39.50 in) in a span of 24 hours which has now become its highest single day record for the month of June and for its all-time single day record, beating its former record of 944.7 mm (37.19 in) on 7 June 1966.

sections.title: Location
sections.content: Location[edit] Mawsynram Climate chart (explanation) J F M A M J J A S O N D     17     16 7     30     17 9     163     21 12     451     22 15     1083     23 16     2348     22 18     2467     22 18     1714     23 18     853     23 18     338     22 15     52     19 11     11     17 8 █ Average max. and min. temperatures in °C █ Precipitation totals in mm Imperial conversion JFMAMJJASOND     0.7     60 44     1.2     62 48     6.4     69 54     18     72 58     43     73 61     92     72 64     97     72 64     67     73 64     34     73 64     13     72 60     2     67 52     0.4     62 46 █ Average max. and min. temperatures in °F █ Precipitation totals in inches Mawsynram is located at 25° 18′ N, 91° 35′ E, at an altitude of about 1,400 meters (4,600 ft), 15 km west of Cherrapunji, in the Khasi Hills in the state of Meghalaya (India). Climate and rainfall[edit] Under the Köppen climate classification, Mawsynram features a subtropical highland climate (Cwb) with an extraordinarily showery, rainy and long monsoonal season and a short dry season. Based on the data of a recent few decades, it appears to be the wettest place in the world, or the place with the highest average annual rainfall.[1] Mawsynram receives over 10,000 millimetres or 390 inches of rain in an average year, and the vast majority of the rain it gets falls during the monsoon months. A comparison of rainfalls for Cherrapunji and Mawsynram for some years is given in Table 1.[2] Mawsynram receives the highest rainfall in India. Although it is reportedly the wettest place on Earth, with an average annual rainfall of 11,872 millimetres (467.4 in), this claim is disputed by Lloró, Colombia, which reported an average yearly rainfall of 12,717 millimetres (500.7 in) between 1952 and 1989 and López de Micay, also in Colombia, which reported 12,892 millimetres (507.6 in) per year between 1960 and 2012. According to the records observed by the Indian Meteorological Department, it was seen that while its neighbour, Cherrapunji is having a significant decreasing trend in rainfall, Mawsynram on the other hand is experiencing a slight increase in its rainfall pattern which put its average annual rainfall from 1950 to 2000 at 12,393 millimetres (487.9 in) and from 2000 to 2020 at 12,120 millimetres (477.2 in). sections.content: Location[edit] Mawsynram Climate chart (explanation) J F M A M J J A S O N D     17     16 7     30     17 9     163     21 12     451     22 15     1083     23 16     2348     22 18     2467     22 18     1714     23 18     853     23 18     338     22 15     52     19 11     11     17 8 █ Average max. and min. temperatures in °C █ Precipitation totals in mm Imperial conversion JFMAMJJASOND     0.7     60 44     1.2     62 48     6.4     69 54     18     72 58     43     73 61     92     72 64     97     72 64     67     73 64     34     73 64     13     72 60     2     67 52     0.4     62 46 █ Average max. and min. temperatures in °F █ Precipitation totals in inches Mawsynram is located at 25° 18′ N, 91° 35′ E, at an altitude of about 1,400 meters (4,600 ft), 15 km west of Cherrapunji, in the Khasi Hills in the state of Meghalaya (India). Climate and rainfall[edit] Under the Köppen climate classification, Mawsynram features a subtropical highland climate (Cwb) with an extraordinarily showery, rainy and long monsoonal season and a short dry season. Based on the data of a recent few decades, it appears to be the wettest place in the world, or the place with the highest average annual rainfall.[1] Mawsynram receives over 10,000 millimetres or 390 inches of rain in an average year, and the vast majority of the rain it gets falls during the monsoon months. A comparison of rainfalls for Cherrapunji and Mawsynram for some years is given in Table 1.[2] Mawsynram receives the highest rainfall in India. Although it is reportedly the wettest place on Earth, with an average annual rainfall of 11,872 millimetres (467.4 in), this claim is disputed by Lloró, Colombia, which reported an average yearly rainfall of 12,717 millimetres (500.7 in) between 1952 and 1989 and López de Micay, also in Colombia, which reported 12,892 millimetres (507.6 in) per year between 1960 and 2012. According to the records observed by the Indian Meteorological Department, it was seen that while its neighbour, Cherrapunji is having a significant decreasing trend in rainfall, Mawsynram on the other hand is experiencing a slight increase in its rainfall pattern which put its average annual rainfall from 1950 to 2000 at 12,393 millimetres (487.9 in) and from 2000 to 2020 at 12,120 millimetres (477.2 in). The precipitation table below shows the average monthly record from 1950 to 2000. Average monthly temperatures range from around 11 °C (51.8 °F) in January to just above 20 °C (68 °F) in August. The village also experiences a brief but noticeably drier season from December until February, when monthly precipitation on average does not exceed 30 millimetres (1.2 in). The little precipitation during the village's "low sun" season is something that is shared by many areas with this type of climate. Climate and rainfall[edit] Under the Köppen climate classification, Mawsynram features a subtropical highland climate (Cwb) with an extraordinarily showery, rainy and long monsoonal season and a short dry season. Based on the data of a recent few decades, it appears to be the wettest place in the world, or the place with the highest average annual rainfall.[1] Mawsynram receives over 10,000 millimetres or 390 inches of rain in an average year, and the vast majority of the rain it gets falls during the monsoon months. A comparison of rainfalls for Cherrapunji and Mawsynram for some years is given in Table 1.[2] Mawsynram receives the highest rainfall in India. Although it is reportedly the wettest place on Earth, with an average annual rainfall of 11,872 millimetres (467.4 in), this claim is disputed by Lloró, Colombia, which reported an average yearly rainfall of 12,717 millimetres (500.7 in) between 1952 and 1989 and López de Micay, also in Colombia, which reported 12,892 millimetres (507.6 in) per year between 1960 and 2012. According to the records observed by the Indian Meteorological Department, it was seen that while its neighbour, Cherrapunji is having a significant decreasing trend in rainfall, Mawsynram on the other hand is experiencing a slight increase in its rainfall pattern which put its average annual rainfall from 1950 to 2000 at 12,393 millimetres (487.9 in) and from 2000 to 2020 at 12,120 millimetres (477.2 in). answer:
The **虎尾驛** (Tigertail Station), originally known as **五間厝驛**, is a historical building located in Yunlin County, Taiwan. It was a former sugar railway station that played a significant role in the development of the Tigertail town area. Today, it is recognized as a historical site and no longer serves transportation purposes.

### Key Information:
- **Name**: 虎尾驛 (Tigertail Station)
- **Location**: Yunlin County, Taiwan
- **Category**: Attraction
- **Popularity**: Moderate (0.7)
- **Historical Significance**: The station was established to facilitate the sugar industry and contributed to the formation of the Tigertail town area.

### Historical Summary:
虎尾驛, originally known as 五間厝驛, is located at the Tigertail Sugar Factory in Yunlin County. It was instrumental in promoting the development of the Tigertail urban area. The original station building is now listed as a historical building in Yunlin County.

### Additional Resources:
For more detailed information, you can visit the [Wikipedia page](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%99%8E%E5%B0%BE%E9%A9%9B).

query: Sualkuchi is a census town in Assam, India, known for its handloom industry and silk production. It is often referred to as the 'Manchester of Assam' due to its significant textile center.
answer:
Here are some attractions related to Sualkuchi, Assam, which is known for its handloom industry and silk production:

1. **Sualkuchi**
   - **Category**: Attraction
   - **Description**: Sualkuchi is a census town in Kamrup district in Assam, located on the north bank of the Brahmaputra River, about 35 km from Guwahati. It is famous for its handloom industry, earning it the nickname "Manchester of Assam."
   - **Visual Tags**: Cityscape, panoramic views, sunny, crowded.
   - **Historical Summary**: Sualkuchi is known for its significant textile center, with many cottage industries engaged in handloom weaving.
   - **Source**: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sualkuchi)

2. **Rupnagar**
   - **Category**: Attraction
   - **Description**: A city in Punjab, known for its historical significance and as a site of the Indus Valley civilization.
   - **Visual Tags**: Cityscape, sunny.

3. **Amarkantak**
   - **Category**: Attraction
   - **Description**: A pilgrim town in Madhya Pradesh, known for its natural heritage and the origin of several rivers.
   - **Visual Tags**: Mountain, valley, lake, cityscape.

4. **Sohra (Cherrapunji)**
   - **Category**: Attraction
   - **Description**: Famous for its heavy rainfall and scenic beauty, located in Meghalaya.
   - **Visual Tags**: Mountain, valley, cityscape, park.

5. **Shillong**
   - **Category**: Attraction
   - **Description**: The capital of Meghalaya, known for its rolling hills and referred to as the "Scotland of the East."
   - **Visual Tags**: Cityscape, mountain, park.

### Summary
Sualkuchi is a significant cultural and historical site in Assam, particularly noted for its textile production. The other attractions listed provide a broader context of nearby places that may also be of interest. If you would like more details about any specific location or need further assistance, feel free to ask!

wikipedia.title: 湖口老街
wikipedia.extract: 湖口老街是位在臺灣新竹縣湖口鄉的一條街道，其中包括街頭、橫街、新街三條街。其興衰與鐵路密切相關，這一帶因為劉銘傳所鋪設的鐵路延伸至此，設有「大湖口火車碼頭」而繁榮，並在日治時期整建成今日風貌，但後來因為鐵路路線調整，「湖口驛」移到下北勢而使街道商業衰退。街道上有新竹縣縣定古蹟湖口三元宮與歷史建築老湖口天主堂，而湖口天主堂即是在舊車站原址上建造而成。近年來經由居民與政府社區總體營造之下，翻修老街牌樓、店亭、石板路與綠化工程，湖口老街有了新風貌。
wikipedia.extract_text: 湖口老街是位在臺灣新竹縣湖口鄉的一條街道，其中包括街頭、橫街、新街三條街。其興衰與鐵路密切相關，這一帶因為劉銘傳所鋪設的鐵路延伸至此，設有「大湖口火車碼頭」而繁榮，並在日治時期整建成今日風貌，但後來因為鐵路路線調整，「湖口驛」移到下北勢而使街道商業衰退。街道上有新竹縣縣定古蹟湖口三元宮與歷史建築老湖口天主堂，而湖口天主堂即是在舊車站原址上建造而成。近年來經由居民與政府社區總體營造之下，翻修老街牌樓、店亭、石板路與綠化工程，湖口老街有了新風貌。

sections.title: 沿革
sections.content: 沿革[编辑] 大湖口驛原址位於湖口老街上的老湖口天主堂，因昭和四年（1929年）鐵路改線後所廢棄。 湖口老街豐瑞（左一）與興泉（左二） 拱圈內的湖口老街豐瑞（左一）與興泉（左二） 湖口地區舊稱「大湖口」或「大窩口」，原是平埔族竹塹社屯墾地，清乾隆時期開始有漢人進入開墾[1]。此地因為是台地與山區的交界，而發展成貨物集散地[2]，後來光緒十八年（1892年）鐵路鋪設到老湖口[註 1]，更是促進了當地的發展。光緒十九年（1893年）正式通車後，新竹與基隆間每天約有六班車，平均每天載客量為400人[1]。 後來進入日治時期後，日本大幅變動臺北到桃園間的鐵路路線，但桃園經大湖口到新竹間的路段則未有太大變化。後來明治四十一年（1908年）縱貫鐵路全線完工後，大湖口便成為了新竹北部的商業重鎮[3]。由於「湖口驛」一帶日益繁榮，當地以羅氏家族為主的鄉紳與富商遂在大正五年（1916年）[註 2]開始在車站東南興建起今天的湖口老街[3][1]，當時稱為「新街」，以與湖口地區已有的「老街」、「橫街」區分[2]。大正七年（1917年）時，村民還配合新街走向重建了三元宮[註 3][1]。 然而在昭和四年（1929年），日人認為楊梅到湖口間路段坡度過陡且路基不穩，便將鐵路路線改從楊梅以西丘地，途經伯公岡（富岡）而到下北勢的新站。自此人潮便流向數公里遠的新湖口，老湖口因而沒落，但老街的風貌也因此完整保留[3]。 近年來透過營建署、文建會等政府單位的援助，湖口老街居民統合地方力量並積極於社區總體營造，目前已完成管線地下化以及整體綠化工程，並且把地面翻修為成適合步行的石板路，而且老街牌樓以及店亭也整修完畢[4]。老街居民因取得天主教會信任，長期借用教堂的部分空間，以傳統宗教公益組織架構，設立了大窩口促進會[4]。 ^ 1.0 1.1 1.2 1.3 1.4 引用错误：没有为名为湖的参考文献提供内容 ^ 2.0 2.1 引用错误：没有为名为黃的参考文献提供内容 ^ 3.0 3.1 3.2 3.3 引用错误：没有为名为沈的参考文献提供内容 ^ 4.0 4.1 引用错误：没有为名为知的参考文献提供内容 引用错误：页面中存在<ref group="註">标签，但没有找到相应的<references group="註" />标签

sections.title: 街景建築
sections.content: 街景建築[编辑] 湖口老街以三元宮為轉折點，主要部分呈現「L」型。短邊位於廟北，長約120公尺；長邊位於廟西，長約640公尺[1]。建築多為磚造牆面，正面一樓為單拱，二樓則開有三扇拱型或方形的窗戶[2]。在臺灣老街之中，此處的騎樓與拱圈較為寬廣，約有4到5公尺，而其外觀裝飾不多，可能與當地居民多為客家人有關[1]。 ^ 1.0 1.1 引用错误：没有为名为湖的参考文献提供内容 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为沈的参考文献提供内容

sections.title: 人文風情
sections.content: 人文風情[编辑] 當地的宗教信仰主要為在老街尾端的三元宮，主祀三官大帝，還供奉有觀音菩薩、媽祖、註生娘娘與伯公（即土地公）等神[1]。另外還有有幾座不同姓氏的家廟與天主教堂[2]，天主教因教友人數減少，天主堂便在1993年停止活動，並閒置下來。直到後來大窩口促進會獲得文建會補助下，將閒置的天主堂改建成文物館[3]。 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为沈的参考文献提供内容 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为旅的参考文献提供内容 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为窩的参考文献提供内容

wikipedia.title: 湖口老街
wikipedia.extract: 湖口老街是位在臺灣新竹縣湖口鄉的一條街道，其中包括街頭、橫街、新街三條街。其興衰與鐵路密切相關，這一帶因為劉銘傳所鋪設的鐵路延伸至此，設有「大湖口火車碼頭」而繁榮，並在日治時期整建成今日風貌，但後來因為鐵路路線調整，「湖口驛」移到下北勢而使街道商業衰退。街道上有新竹縣縣定古蹟湖口三元宮與歷史建築老湖口天主堂，而湖口天主堂即是在舊車站原址上建造而成。近年來經由居民與政府社區總體營造之下，翻修老街牌樓、店亭、石板路與綠化工程，湖口老街有了新風貌。
wikipedia.extract_text: 湖口老街是位在臺灣新竹縣湖口鄉的一條街道，其中包括街頭、橫街、新街三條街。其興衰與鐵路密切相關，這一帶因為劉銘傳所鋪設的鐵路延伸至此，設有「大湖口火車碼頭」而繁榮，並在日治時期整建成今日風貌，但後來因為鐵路路線調整，「湖口驛」移到下北勢而使街道商業衰退。街道上有新竹縣縣定古蹟湖口三元宮與歷史建築老湖口天主堂，而湖口天主堂即是在舊車站原址上建造而成。近年來經由居民與政府社區總體營造之下，翻修老街牌樓、店亭、石板路與綠化工程，湖口老街有了新風貌。

sections.title: 沿革
sections.content: 沿革[编辑] 大湖口驛原址位於湖口老街上的老湖口天主堂，因昭和四年（1929年）鐵路改線後所廢棄。 湖口老街豐瑞（左一）與興泉（左二） 拱圈內的湖口老街豐瑞（左一）與興泉（左二） 湖口地區舊稱「大湖口」或「大窩口」，原是平埔族竹塹社屯墾地，清乾隆時期開始有漢人進入開墾[1]。此地因為是台地與山區的交界，而發展成貨物集散地[2]，後來光緒十八年（1892年）鐵路鋪設到老湖口[註 1]，更是促進了當地的發展。光緒十九年（1893年）正式通車後，新竹與基隆間每天約有六班車，平均每天載客量為400人[1]。 後來進入日治時期後，日本大幅變動臺北到桃園間的鐵路路線，但桃園經大湖口到新竹間的路段則未有太大變化。後來明治四十一年（1908年）縱貫鐵路全線完工後，大湖口便成為了新竹北部的商業重鎮[3]。由於「湖口驛」一帶日益繁榮，當地以羅氏家族為主的鄉紳與富商遂在大正五年（1916年）[註 2]開始在車站東南興建起今天的湖口老街[3][1]，當時稱為「新街」，以與湖口地區已有的「老街」、「橫街」區分[2]。大正七年（1917年）時，村民還配合新街走向重建了三元宮[註 3][1]。 然而在昭和四年（1929年），日人認為楊梅到湖口間路段坡度過陡且路基不穩，便將鐵路路線改從楊梅以西丘地，途經伯公岡（富岡）而到下北勢的新站。自此人潮便流向數公里遠的新湖口，老湖口因而沒落，但老街的風貌也因此完整保留[3]。 近年來透過營建署、文建會等政府單位的援助，湖口老街居民統合地方力量並積極於社區總體營造，目前已完成管線地下化以及整體綠化工程，並且把地面翻修為成適合步行的石板路，而且老街牌樓以及店亭也整修完畢[4]。老街居民因取得天主教會信任，長期借用教堂的部分空間，以傳統宗教公益組織架構，設立了大窩口促進會[4]。 ^ 1.0 1.1 1.2 1.3 1.4 引用错误：没有为名为湖的参考文献提供内容 ^ 2.0 2.1 引用错误：没有为名为黃的参考文献提供内容 ^ 3.0 3.1 3.2 3.3 引用错误：没有为名为沈的参考文献提供内容 ^ 4.0 4.1 引用错误：没有为名为知的参考文献提供内容 引用错误：页面中存在<ref group="註">标签，但没有找到相应的<references group="註" />标签

sections.title: 街景建築
sections.content: 街景建築[编辑] 湖口老街以三元宮為轉折點，主要部分呈現「L」型。短邊位於廟北，長約120公尺；長邊位於廟西，長約640公尺[1]。建築多為磚造牆面，正面一樓為單拱，二樓則開有三扇拱型或方形的窗戶[2]。在臺灣老街之中，此處的騎樓與拱圈較為寬廣，約有4到5公尺，而其外觀裝飾不多，可能與當地居民多為客家人有關[1]。 ^ 1.0 1.1 引用错误：没有为名为湖的参考文献提供内容 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为沈的参考文献提供内容

sections.title: 人文風情
sections.content: 人文風情[编辑] 當地的宗教信仰主要為在老街尾端的三元宮，主祀三官大帝，還供奉有觀音菩薩、媽祖、註生娘娘與伯公（即土地公）等神[1]。另外還有有幾座不同姓氏的家廟與天主教堂[2]，天主教因教友人數減少，天主堂便在1993年停止活動，並閒置下來。直到後來大窩口促進會獲得文建會補助下，將閒置的天主堂改建成文物館[3]。 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为沈的参考文献提供内容 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为旅的参考文献提供内容 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为窩的参考文献提供内容

wikipedia.title: 湖口老街
wikipedia.extract: 湖口老街是位在臺灣新竹縣湖口鄉的一條街道，其中包括街頭、橫街、新街三條街。其興衰與鐵路密切相關，這一帶因為劉銘傳所鋪設的鐵路延伸至此，設有「大湖口火車碼頭」而繁榮，並在日治時期整建成今日風貌，但後來因為鐵路路線調整，「湖口驛」移到下北勢而使街道商業衰退。街道上有新竹縣縣定古蹟湖口三元宮與歷史建築老湖口天主堂，而湖口天主堂即是在舊車站原址上建造而成。近年來經由居民與政府社區總體營造之下，翻修老街牌樓、店亭、石板路與綠化工程，湖口老街有了新風貌。

sections.title: 沿革
sections.content: 沿革[编辑] 大湖口驛原址位於湖口老街上的老湖口天主堂，因昭和四年（1929年）鐵路改線後所廢棄。 湖口老街豐瑞（左一）與興泉（左二） 拱圈內的湖口老街豐瑞（左一）與興泉（左二） 湖口地區舊稱「大湖口」或「大窩口」，原是平埔族竹塹社屯墾地，清乾隆時期開始有漢人進入開墾[1]。此地因為是台地與山區的交界，而發展成貨物集散地[2]，後來光緒十八年（1892年）鐵路鋪設到老湖口[註 1]，更是促進了當地的發展。光緒十九年（1893年）正式通車後，新竹與基隆間每天約有六班車，平均每天載客量為400人[1]。 後來進入日治時期後，日本大幅變動臺北到桃園間的鐵路路線，但桃園經大湖口到新竹間的路段則未有太大變化。後來明治四十一年（1908年）縱貫鐵路全線完工後，大湖口便成為了新竹北部的商業重鎮[3]。由於「湖口驛」一帶日益繁榮，當地以羅氏家族為主的鄉紳與富商遂在大正五年（1916年）[註 2]開始在車站東南興建起今天的湖口老街[3][1]，當時稱為「新街」，以與湖口地區已有的「老街」、「橫街」區分[2]。大正七年（1917年）時，村民還配合新街走向重建了三元宮[註 3][1]。 然而在昭和四年（1929年），日人認為楊梅到湖口間路段坡度過陡且路基不穩，便將鐵路路線改從楊梅以西丘地，途經伯公岡（富岡）而到下北勢的新站。自此人潮便流向數公里遠的新湖口，老湖口因而沒落，但老街的風貌也因此完整保留[3]。 近年來透過營建署、文建會等政府單位的援助，湖口老街居民統合地方力量並積極於社區總體營造，目前已完成管線地下化以及整體綠化工程，並且把地面翻修為成適合步行的石板路，而且老街牌樓以及店亭也整修完畢[4]。老街居民因取得天主教會信任，長期借用教堂的部分空間，以傳統宗教公益組織架構，設立了大窩口促進會[4]。 ^ 1.0 1.1 1.2 1.3 1.4 引用错误：没有为名为湖的参考文献提供内容 ^ 2.0 2.1 引用错误：没有为名为黃的参考文献提供内容 ^ 3.0 3.1 3.2 3.3 引用错误：没有为名为沈的参考文献提供内容 ^ 4.0 4.1 引用错误：没有为名为知的参考文献提供内容 引用错误：页面中存在<ref group="註">标签，但没有找到相应的<references group="註" />标签

sections.title: 街景建築
sections.content: 街景建築[编辑] 湖口老街以三元宮為轉折點，主要部分呈現「L」型。短邊位於廟北，長約120公尺；長邊位於廟西，長約640公尺[1]。建築多為磚造牆面，正面一樓為單拱，二樓則開有三扇拱型或方形的窗戶[2]。在臺灣老街之中，此處的騎樓與拱圈較為寬廣，約有4到5公尺，而其外觀裝飾不多，可能與當地居民多為客家人有關[1]。 ^ 1.0 1.1 引用错误：没有为名为湖的参考文献提供内容 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为沈的参考文献提供内容

sections.title: 人文風情
sections.content: 人文風情[编辑] 當地的宗教信仰主要為在老街尾端的三元宮，主祀三官大帝，還供奉有觀音菩薩、媽祖、註生娘娘與伯公（即土地公）等神[1]。另外還有有幾座不同姓氏的家廟與天主教堂[2]，天主教因教友人數減少，天主堂便在1993年停止活動，並閒置下來。直到後來大窩口促進會獲得文建會補助下，將閒置的天主堂改建成文物館[3]。 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为沈的参考文献提供内容 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为旅的参考文献提供内容 ^ 引用错误：没有为名为窩的参考文献提供内容

query: Muktinath is an ancient Vishnu temple located in Mustang, Nepal, revered by both Hindus and Buddhists. It is one of the highest temples in the world, situated at an altitude of 3,800 meters, and is considered a sacred site for liberation.
answer:
Muktinath is an ancient Vishnu temple located in Mustang, Nepal, revered by both Hindus and Buddhists. Here are some key details about this sacred site:

- **Altitude**: Muktinath is situated at an impressive altitude of 3,800 meters, making it one of the highest temples in the world.
- **Religious Significance**: Known as "the lord of liberation," Muktinath is considered a sacred site for both Hindus and Buddhists. Hindus worship it as an abode of the deity Vishnu, while Buddhists regard it as a sacred place associated with Avalokiteśvara.
- **Cultural Importance**: The temple is recognized as one of the 108 Divya Desams of Sri Vaishnavism and is also one of the eight most sacred shrines in that tradition, known as the Svayam Vyakta Ksetras. Additionally, it is one of the 51 Shakta pithas, linked to the head of goddess Sati.
- **Mukti Kshetra**: The temple complex is referred to as Mukti Kshetra, which translates to "the place of liberation (moksha)," and it is one of the Char Dham in Nepal.

For more information, you can visit the [Wikipedia page on Muktinath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muktinath).

![Muktinath](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A5_%28Muktinath%29.jpg/800px-%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A5_%28Muktinath%29.jpg)

query: Furfura Sharif is a significant pilgrimage site in West Bengal, India, known for its mazar of Pir Mohammad Abu Bakr Siddique. The site attracts many visitors during the Urs festival and is revered by both Hindus and Muslims.
answer:
### Furfura Sharif Overview

**Furfura Sharif** is a significant pilgrimage site located in the Hooghly District of West Bengal, India. It is renowned for the mazar (shrine) of **Pir Mohammad Abu Bakr Siddique**, a prominent figure in the region. This site is particularly revered by both Hindus and Muslims and attracts many visitors, especially during the **Urs festival**.

#### Key Details:
- **Location**: Furfura, Jangipara community development block, Srirampore subdivision, Hooghly District, West Bengal, India.
- **Historical Significance**: 
  - The site is considered the second most prominent mazar in West Bengal, following Gazi Pir Mazar in Ghutiari Sharif.
  - The shrine was established in honor of Pir Mohammad Abu Bakr Siddique (1846–1939), who was a social and religious reformer.
  - The area is known for its historical mosque built by Muqlish Khan in 1375, which serves as a pilgrimage site, particularly during the pir's mela (fair).

#### Visitor Experience:
- **Crowds**: The site is often crowded, especially during religious ceremonies and festivals.
- **Activities**: Visitors can participate in prayers and ceremonies at the mazar, and the site is known for its vibrant atmosphere during the Urs festival.

#### Additional Information:
- **Wikipedia**: For more detailed historical context and visitor information, you can visit the [Wikipedia page on Furfura Sharif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Furfura_Sharif).

#### Visual Tags:
- The site is characterized by its exterior architecture, often bustling with activity during festivals, and surrounded by lush greenery in the summer and spring seasons.

If you have any specific questions or need further assistance regarding Furfura Sharif or its surroundings, feel free to ask!

wikipedia.extract: Furfura is a village in Jangipara community development block of Srirampore subdivision in Hooghly District in the state of West Bengal, India. It is a holy place for some Bengali Muslims. Before the afternoon prayers, people queue up at the mazar (shrine) of Mohammad Abu Bakr Siddique (1846–1939), a prominent pir of the town. People say it is the second most prominent mazar in west bengal after Gazi Pir Mazar in Ghutiari Sharif.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] The masjid built by Muqlish Khan in 1375 is a site for Muslim pilgrimage, especially during the pir's mela (fair).[1] It attracts a large number of pilgrims during Urs festival.[2] Oral tradition holds that the Bagdi (Barga Kshatriya) king who ruled here was defeated by Shah Kabir Halibi and Karamuddin, both of whom were killed in the battle.[3] Their tombs are revered to this day by both Hindus and Muslims.[3] Veracity of the account and other details are unstudied.[4] Furfura Sharif contains the mazar of one Pir Mohammad Abu Bakr Siddique and his five sons, popularly known as the Panch Huzur Qeblah.[5] He was a social and religious reformer, who founded charitable institutes, orphanages, madrasas, schools and learning centers. He encouraged female education by establishing a School for girls in Furfura Sharif named Siddiqua High School. He was the founder of the "Order Of Furfura Sharif" or "Silsila-e-Furfura Sharif" and a religious congregation observed on the 21st 22nd and 23rd of Falgun Bengali month (Approx 5, 6 & 7 March).[6][7] sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] The masjid built by Muqlish Khan in 1375 is a site for Muslim pilgrimage, especially during the pir's mela (fair).[1] It attracts a large number of pilgrims during Urs festival.[2] Oral tradition holds that the Bagdi (Barga Kshatriya) king who ruled here was defeated by Shah Kabir Halibi and Karamuddin, both of whom were killed in the battle.[3] Their tombs are revered to this day by both Hindus and Muslims.[3] Veracity of the account and other details are unstudied.[4] Furfura Sharif contains the mazar of one Pir Mohammad Abu Bakr Siddique and his five sons, popularly known as the Panch Huzur Qeblah.[5] He was a social and religious reformer, who founded charitable institutes, orphanages, madrasas, schools and learning centers. He encouraged female education by establishing a School for girls in Furfura Sharif named Siddiqua High School. He was the founder of the "Order Of Furfura Sharif" or "Silsila-e-Furfura Sharif" and a religious congregation observed on the 21st 22nd and 23rd of Falgun Bengali month (Approx 5, 6 & 7 March).[6][7] query: Lal Chowk is a prominent city square in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, serving as the main business district since the early twentieth century. It features a traffic roundabout and a clock tower constructed in 1980.
answer:
**Lal Chowk** is a significant city square located in **Srinagar**, in the Indian union territory of **Jammu and Kashmir**. It has served as the main business district since the early twentieth century and features a traffic roundabout along with a clock tower constructed in 1980.

### Key Information:
- **Category**: Attraction
- **Popularity**: Moderate (0.7)
- **Description**: Lal Chowk stretches on both sides of the Residency Road between the Amira Kadal bridge and the Tyndale Biscoe School. It has evolved into Srinagar's main business district and houses a notable clock tower (ganta ghar) built by Bajaj Electricals in 1980.

### Historical Significance:
- **1948**: The square is historically significant as it was the location where **Jawaharlal Nehru**, the first Prime Minister of India, unfurled the Indian national flag shortly after India gained independence.
- **1990s**: The area has seen various political events, including challenges to raise the Indian flag during times of unrest.
- **Recent Events**: In January 2023, **Rahul Gandhi** unfurled the national tricolor here as part of the Bharat Jodo Yatra.

### Visual Tags:
- **Tags**: exterior, cityscape, crowded, ground level, panoramic, sunny
- **Location**: India

For more detailed information, you can visit the [Wikipedia page on Lal Chowk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lal_Chowk).

If you have any specific questions or need further assistance regarding Lal Chowk or other attractions, feel free to ask!

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] Sheikh Abdullah speaking at Lal Chowk in 1975 Lal Chowk was the location where Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India, unfurled the Indian national flag in 1948, shortly after the country gained independence from the British Empire.[1] Following the Indo-Pakistani War of 1947–1948, Nehru stood in Lal Chowk and promised the Kashmiri people a chance to vote in a referendum whereby they would be able to choose their political future. The city square was also the location where Sheikh Abdullah, the first elected Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, expressed his allegiance to Nehru and India in a Persian couplet, saying "Man Tu Shudam, Tu Man Shudi, Taqas Na Goyed, Man Degram Tu Degri (I became you and you became I; so none can say we are separate)".[1] 1990s[edit] In 1990, separatists had dared anyone to try and raise the flag of India at Lal Chowk. The National Security Guards took up the challenge and raised the flag.[1] The clock tower gained political significance in 1992, when the then Bharatiya Janata Party president, Murli Manohar Joshi, hoisted the Indian flag on top of the tower on Republic Day.[2][3] Joshi hoisted the flag in the company of Indian troops. However, some BJP activists reached Srinagar and hoisted the Indian flag near the city square, although they failed to reach their intended destination on top of the clock tower.[13] Sushma Swaraj, upon her arrest by security forces, said: "Why are we being arrested? We were marching peacefully. query: The Taiwan Times Village is a museum located in Caotun Township, Nantou County, Taiwan. It showcases the past life of Taiwan, including the cultures of Hakka, Hoklo, Taiwanese aborigines, and veterans from Mainland China.
answer:
The **Taiwan Times Village** (寶島時代村) is a museum located in **Caotun Township**, **Nantou County**, **Taiwan**. It showcases the rich cultural heritage and past life of Taiwan, including the traditions and lifestyles of the Hakka, Hoklo, Taiwanese aborigines, and veterans from Mainland China.

### Key Information:
- **Category**: Museum
- **Popularity Score**: 0.7 (indicating a moderate level of visitor interest)
- **Transportation**: The museum is accessible from Highway 3.

### Exhibitions:
The museum features various exhibitions that represent different community blocks, highlighting the diverse cultures and histories of Taiwan's inhabitants.

### Additional Resources:
- For more detailed information, you can visit the [Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan_Times_Village).

If you have any specific questions or need further assistance, feel free to ask!

query: The Third Tunnel of Aggression is one of four known tunnels under the border between North Korea and South Korea, discovered in 1978. It was allegedly designed for a surprise attack on Seoul and is considered an act of aggression by South Korea.
answer:
Here are some notable attractions related to the Third Tunnel of Aggression and the historical context of the Korean peninsula:

1. **Third Tunnel of Aggression (제3땅굴)**
   - **Description**: The Third Tunnel of Aggression is one of four known tunnels under the border between North Korea and South Korea, extending south of Panmunjom. It was discovered in 1978 and is believed to have been designed for a surprise attack on Seoul. The tunnel is approximately 1,635 meters long and was capable of accommodating 30,000 troops per hour.
   - **Tourist Information**: The tunnel is now a tourist site, accessible via a steep incline or a rubber-tyred train. Photography is prohibited inside the tunnel, and visitors can only go as far as the third barricade.
   - **Wikipedia Link**: [Third Tunnel of Aggression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Tunnel_of_Aggression)

2. **Longmen Caves (龙门洞)**
   - **Description**: This site is known for its historical significance and beautiful cave formations. It is located in Yongsan District, Seoul, South Korea.
   - **Wikipedia Link**: [Longmen Caves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yongmun-dong)

3. **Namsangol Hanok Village (남산골한옥마을)**
   - **Description**: A recreated village of historical Korean buildings, Namsangol Hanok Village features several traditional houses called hanok. It is located in Pil-dong, Jung District, Seoul, and offers a glimpse into Korea's architectural heritage.
   - **Wikipedia Link**: [Namsangol Hanok Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namsangol_Hanok_Village)

4. **Samjeondo Monument (서울 삼전도비)**
   - **Description**: This monument marks the submission of the Korean Joseon dynasty to the Manchu-led Qing dynasty in 1636. It is designated as the 101st historic site of South Korea.
   - **Wikipedia Link**: [Samjeondo Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samjeondo_Monument)

5. **Mongchontoseong Earthen Fortification (몽촌토성)**
   - **Description**: An ancient earthen rampart dating from the Baekje period, located in what is now Olympic Park in Seoul. It is a significant historical site reflecting Korea's ancient fortifications.
   - **Wikipedia Link**: [Mongchontoseong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongch'ont'os%C5%8Dng)

These sites provide a rich historical context and are significant attractions for those interested in the history and culture of Korea.

sections.title: Background
sections.content: Background[edit] Aggression tunnels on the Koreas border Only 44 km (27 miles) from Seoul, the incomplete tunnel was discovered in October 1978 following the detection of an underground explosion in June 1978, apparently caused by the tunnellers who had progressed 435 metres (1,427 feet) under the south side of the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). It took four months to locate the tunnel precisely and dig an intercept tunnel.[1][2] The incomplete tunnel is 1,635 metres (1.0 mile) long, 1.95 m (6 ft 5 in) at its maximum height and 2.1 m (6 ft 11 in) wide.[2] It runs through bedrock at a depth of about 73 m (240 ft) below ground.[2] It was apparently designed for a surprise attack on Seoul from North Korea, and could, according to visitor information in the tunnel, accommodate 30,000 men per hour along with light weaponry.[3] Upon discovery of the third tunnel, the United Nations Command accused North Korea of threatening the 1953 Korean Armistice Agreement signed at the end of the Korean War.[4] Its description as a "tunnel of aggression" was given by South Korea, who considered it an act of aggression on the part of North Korea. Initially, North Korea denied building the tunnel.[5] North Korea then declared it part of a coal mine,[6] the tunnel having been blackened by construction explosions.[2] Signs in the tunnel claim that there is no geological likelihood of coal being in the area. The walls of the tunnel where tourists are taken are observably granite, a stone of igneous origin, whereas coal would be found in stone of sedimentary origin.[1] A total of four tunnels have been discovered so far, but there are believed to be up to twenty more.[7] The South Korean Armed Forces still devotes specialist resources to finding infiltration tunnels, though tunnels are much less significant now that North Korean long-range artillery and missiles have become more effective.[8] ^ a b .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output sections.content: Tourist site[edit] The tunnel is now a tourist site, though still well guarded.[1] Visitors enter either by walking down a long steep incline that starts in a lobby with a gift shop or via a rubber-tyred train that contains a driver at the front or the back (depending on the direction as there is only one set of rails) and padded seats facing forward and backwards in rows for up to three passengers each.[2] Photography is forbidden within the tunnel.[3] The South Koreans have blocked the actual Military Demarcation Line in the tunnel with three concrete barricades. sections.content: Overview[edit] Yongmun-dong was founded in 1946 and is known for its significant annual celebrations held on April 1 and October 17. Historically, the eastern region of Yongmun-dong boasted a substantial peach orchard planting area.

wikipedia.extract_text: Namsangol Hanok Village (Korean: 남산골한옥마을) is a recreated village of historical Korean buildings in Pil-dong, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea. The village contains several Korean traditional houses called hanok.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] The location of the village was originally the site of a well known Joseon-era summer resort called Jeonghakdong. Jeonghakdong means "The land of the fairies for the blue crane where the Jeonugak Pavilion stands along the stream in the valley". The area boasted such superb scenery that it was called the land of the fairies and was considered one of the five most beautiful parts of Seoul. A traditional Korean style garden, complete with a flowing stream and pavilion was constructed on the site in order to revive the classical feel of the Joseon-era. Five traditional houses, including some of the residences of high government officials - some of the largest mansions in Seoul at the time, along with commoners houses were moved to the 7,934 sq Meters/9,489 sq Yards grounds containing the restored village.

wikipedia.title: 서울_삼전도비
wikipedia.extract: The Samjeondo Monument is a monument marking the submission of the Korean Joseon dynasty to the Manchu-led Qing dynasty in 1636 after the latter's invasion of the former. Its original name was Daecheong Hwangje Gongdeok Bi (大淸皇帝功德碑), which means the stele to the merits and virtues of the Emperor of the Great Qing. Initially erected at Samjeondo, near the Sambatnaru crossing point of the Han River in modern-day Seoul, it was thereafter buried and erected again several times. It is designated as the 101st historic site of South Korea.
wikipedia.extract_text: The Samjeondo Monument is a monument marking the submission of the Korean Joseon dynasty to the Manchu-led Qing dynasty in 1636 after the latter's invasion of the former. Its original name was Daecheong Hwangje Gongdeok Bi (大淸皇帝功德碑), which means the stele to the merits and virtues of the Emperor of the Great Qing. Initially erected at Samjeondo, near the Sambatnaru crossing point of the Han River in modern-day Seoul, it was thereafter buried and erected again several times. It is designated as the 101st historic site of South Korea.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: Description[edit] Both the Qing and Joseon dynasties saw the inscription as the litmus test for the latter's attitude toward the Qing emperor, so King Injo ensured that it flattered the Qing dynasty: the inscription narrates how the king of Joseon came to attach himself to the virtue of the Qing emperor from a Joseon point of view. Although one-sided, it provides a concise account of the Qing-Joseon relationship. The inscription starts with the description of the Qing campaign against Joseon in 1636. The Qing army besieged the Namhan fortress, where King Injo took refuge. He admitted his guilt, accepted the imperial edict and surrendered at Samjeondo. Since Hong Taiji felt compassion for the Joseon king, he mercifully sent the king back to the capital and rapidly withdrew the army without doing harm to the people. In the next paragraph, the inscription traces the history back to the Battle of Sarhū in 1619. The Joseon army, led by Gang Hong-rip, put on the appearance of supporting the Ming dynasty but surrendered to the Qing dynasty. However, all of the soldiers except the high-ranking ones were released by Nurhaci, and the inscription emphasizes the merciful act. Since Joseon still displayed disobedient behavior, Hong Taiji commenced the Later Jin invasion of Joseon in 1627. He did not overthrow the kingdom but established a Confucian "elder brother-younger brother" relationship. The inscription then goes on to describe the second campaign. When Hong Taiji proclaimed the Qing dynasty in 1636, Joseon did not accept it even though Qing China announced a war. The inscription stressed his benevolent acts during the war. Next, the inscription explains the background of erection of the monument. It says that the king voluntarily erected the monument at Samjeondo to let the excellent virtue of the Qing emperor be known around the world. Finally, the inscription summarizes the entire course of events in verse.[1] ^ .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output .citation result.historical_summary: The Samjeondo Monument is a monument marking the submission of the Korean Joseon dynasty to the Manchu-led Qing dynasty in 1636 after the latter's invasion of the former. Its original name was Daecheong Hwangje Gongdeok Bi (大淸皇帝功德碑), which means the stele to the merits and virtues of the Emperor of the Great Qing. Initially erected at Samjeondo, near the Sambatnaru crossing point of the Han River in modern-day Seoul, it was thereafter buried and erected again several times. It is designated as the 101st historic site of South Korea.

wikipedia.extract: The Third Tunnel of Aggression is one of four known tunnels under the border between North Korea and South Korea, extending south of Panmunjom.
wikipedia.extract_text: The Third Tunnel of Aggression is one of four known tunnels under the border between North Korea and South Korea, extending south of Panmunjom.

sections.title: Background
sections.content: Background[edit] Aggression tunnels on the Koreas border Only 44 km (27 miles) from Seoul, the incomplete tunnel was discovered in October 1978 following the detection of an underground explosion in June 1978, apparently caused by the tunnellers who had progressed 435 metres (1,427 feet) under the south side of the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). It took four months to locate the tunnel precisely and dig an intercept tunnel.[1][2] The incomplete tunnel is 1,635 metres (1.0 mile) long, 1.95 m (6 ft 5 in) at its maximum height and 2.1 m (6 ft 11 in) wide.[2] It runs through bedrock at a depth of about 73 m (240 ft) below ground.[2] It was apparently designed for a surprise attack on Seoul from North Korea, and could, according to visitor information in the tunnel, accommodate 30,000 men per hour along with light weaponry.[3] Upon discovery of the third tunnel, the United Nations Command accused North Korea of threatening the 1953 Korean Armistice Agreement signed at the end of the Korean War.[4] Its description as a "tunnel of aggression" was given by South Korea, who considered it an act of aggression on the part of North Korea. Initially, North Korea denied building the tunnel.[5] North Korea then declared it part of a coal mine,[6] the tunnel having been blackened by construction explosions.[2] Signs in the tunnel claim that there is no geological likelihood of coal being in the area. The walls of the tunnel where tourists are taken are observably granite, a stone of igneous origin, whereas coal would be found in stone of sedimentary origin.[1] A total of four tunnels have been discovered so far, but there are believed to be up to twenty more.[7] The South Korean Armed Forces still devotes specialist resources to finding infiltration tunnels, though tunnels are much less significant now that North Korean long-range artillery and missiles have become more effective.[8] ^ a b .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output sections.title: Tourist site
sections.content: Tourist site[edit] The tunnel is now a tourist site, though still well guarded.[1] Visitors enter either by walking down a long steep incline that starts in a lobby with a gift shop or via a rubber-tyred train that contains a driver at the front or the back (depending on the direction as there is only one set of rails) and padded seats facing forward and backwards in rows for up to three passengers each.[2] Photography is forbidden within the tunnel.[3] The South Koreans have blocked the actual Military Demarcation Line in the tunnel with three concrete barricades. Tourists can walk as far as the third barricade, and the second barricade is visible through a small window in the third.[4] ^ .mw-parser-output sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Overview[edit] Yongmun-dong was founded in 1946 and is known for its significant annual celebrations held on April 1 and October 17. Historically, the eastern region of Yongmun-dong boasted a substantial peach orchard planting area.

wikipedia.extract: Namsangol Hanok Village (Korean: 남산골한옥마을) is a recreated village of historical Korean buildings in Pil-dong, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea. The village contains several Korean traditional houses called hanok.
wikipedia.extract_text: Namsangol Hanok Village (Korean: 남산골한옥마을) is a recreated village of historical Korean buildings in Pil-dong, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea. The village contains several Korean traditional houses called hanok.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] The location of the village was originally the site of a well known Joseon-era summer resort called Jeonghakdong. Jeonghakdong means "The land of the fairies for the blue crane where the Jeonugak Pavilion stands along the stream in the valley". The area boasted such superb scenery that it was called the land of the fairies and was considered one of the five most beautiful parts of Seoul. A traditional Korean style garden, complete with a flowing stream and pavilion was constructed on the site in order to revive the classical feel of the Joseon-era. Five traditional houses, including some of the residences of high government officials - some of the largest mansions in Seoul at the time, along with commoners houses were moved to the 7,934 sq Meters/9,489 sq Yards grounds containing the restored village.

wikipedia.title: 서울_삼전도비
wikipedia.extract: The Samjeondo Monument is a monument marking the submission of the Korean Joseon dynasty to the Manchu-led Qing dynasty in 1636 after the latter's invasion of the former. Its original name was Daecheong Hwangje Gongdeok Bi (大淸皇帝功德碑), which means the stele to the merits and virtues of the Emperor of the Great Qing. Initially erected at Samjeondo, near the Sambatnaru crossing point of the Han River in modern-day Seoul, it was thereafter buried and erected again several times. It is designated as the 101st historic site of South Korea.
wikipedia.extract_text: The Samjeondo Monument is a monument marking the submission of the Korean Joseon dynasty to the Manchu-led Qing dynasty in 1636 after the latter's invasion of the former. Its original name was Daecheong Hwangje Gongdeok Bi (大淸皇帝功德碑), which means the stele to the merits and virtues of the Emperor of the Great Qing. Initially erected at Samjeondo, near the Sambatnaru crossing point of the Han River in modern-day Seoul, it was thereafter buried and erected again several times. It is designated as the 101st historic site of South Korea.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: Description[edit] Both the Qing and Joseon dynasties saw the inscription as the litmus test for the latter's attitude toward the Qing emperor, so King Injo ensured that it flattered the Qing dynasty: the inscription narrates how the king of Joseon came to attach himself to the virtue of the Qing emperor from a Joseon point of view. Although one-sided, it provides a concise account of the Qing-Joseon relationship. The inscription starts with the description of the Qing campaign against Joseon in 1636. The Qing army besieged the Namhan fortress, where King Injo took refuge. He admitted his guilt, accepted the imperial edict and surrendered at Samjeondo. Since Hong Taiji felt compassion for the Joseon king, he mercifully sent the king back to the capital and rapidly withdrew the army without doing harm to the people. In the next paragraph, the inscription traces the history back to the Battle of Sarhū in 1619. The Joseon army, led by Gang Hong-rip, put on the appearance of supporting the Ming dynasty but surrendered to the Qing dynasty. However, all of the soldiers except the high-ranking ones were released by Nurhaci, and the inscription emphasizes the merciful act. Since Joseon still displayed disobedient behavior, Hong Taiji commenced the Later Jin invasion of Joseon in 1627. He did not overthrow the kingdom but established a Confucian "elder brother-younger brother" relationship. The inscription then goes on to describe the second campaign. When Hong Taiji proclaimed the Qing dynasty in 1636, Joseon did not accept it even though Qing China announced a war. The inscription stressed his benevolent acts during the war. Next, the inscription explains the background of erection of the monument. It says that the king voluntarily erected the monument at Samjeondo to let the excellent virtue of the Qing emperor be known around the world. result.historical_summary: The Samjeondo Monument is a monument marking the submission of the Korean Joseon dynasty to the Manchu-led Qing dynasty in 1636 after the latter's invasion of the former. Its original name was Daecheong Hwangje Gongdeok Bi (大淸皇帝功德碑), which means the stele to the merits and virtues of the Emperor of the Great Qing. Initially erected at Samjeondo, near the Sambatnaru crossing point of the Han River in modern-day Seoul, it was thereafter buried and erected again several times. It is designated as the 101st historic site of South Korea.

sections.title: Background
sections.content: Background[edit] Aggression tunnels on the Koreas border Only 44 km (27 miles) from Seoul, the incomplete tunnel was discovered in October 1978 following the detection of an underground explosion in June 1978, apparently caused by the tunnellers who had progressed 435 metres (1,427 feet) under the south side of the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). It took four months to locate the tunnel precisely and dig an intercept tunnel.[1][2] The incomplete tunnel is 1,635 metres (1.0 mile) long, 1.95 m (6 ft 5 in) at its maximum height and 2.1 m (6 ft 11 in) wide.[2] It runs through bedrock at a depth of about 73 m (240 ft) below ground.[2] It was apparently designed for a surprise attack on Seoul from North Korea, and could, according to visitor information in the tunnel, accommodate 30,000 men per hour along with light weaponry.[3] Upon discovery of the third tunnel, the United Nations Command accused North Korea of threatening the 1953 Korean Armistice Agreement signed at the end of the Korean War.[4] Its description as a "tunnel of aggression" was given by South Korea, who considered it an act of aggression on the part of North Korea. Initially, North Korea denied building the tunnel.[5] North Korea then declared it part of a coal mine,[6] the tunnel having been blackened by construction explosions.[2] Signs in the tunnel claim that there is no geological likelihood of coal being in the area. The walls of the tunnel where tourists are taken are observably granite, a stone of igneous origin, whereas coal would be found in stone of sedimentary origin.[1] A total of four tunnels have been discovered so far, but there are believed to be up to twenty more.[7] The South Korean Armed Forces still devotes specialist resources to finding infiltration tunnels, though tunnels are much less significant now that North Korean long-range artillery and missiles have become more effective.[8] ^ a b .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output sections.title: Tourist site
sections.content: Tourist site[edit] The tunnel is now a tourist site, though still well guarded.[1] Visitors enter either by walking down a long steep incline that starts in a lobby with a gift shop or via a rubber-tyred train that contains a driver at the front or the back (depending on the direction as there is only one set of rails) and padded seats facing forward and backwards in rows for up to three passengers each.[2] Photography is forbidden within the tunnel.[3] The South Koreans have blocked the actual Military Demarcation Line in the tunnel with three concrete barricades. Tourists can walk as far as the third barricade, and the second barricade is visible through a small window in the third.[4] ^ .mw-parser-output wikipedia.extract_text: Namsangol Hanok Village (Korean: 남산골한옥마을) is a recreated village of historical Korean buildings in Pil-dong, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea. The village contains several Korean traditional houses called hanok.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] The location of the village was originally the site of a well known Joseon-era summer resort called Jeonghakdong. Jeonghakdong means "The land of the fairies for the blue crane where the Jeonugak Pavilion stands along the stream in the valley". The area boasted such superb scenery that it was called the land of the fairies and was considered one of the five most beautiful parts of Seoul. A traditional Korean style garden, complete with a flowing stream and pavilion was constructed on the site in order to revive the classical feel of the Joseon-era. Five traditional houses, including some of the residences of high government officials - some of the largest mansions in Seoul at the time, along with commoners houses were moved to the 7,934 sq Meters/9,489 sq Yards grounds containing the restored village.

wikipedia.title: 서울_삼전도비
wikipedia.extract: The Samjeondo Monument is a monument marking the submission of the Korean Joseon dynasty to the Manchu-led Qing dynasty in 1636 after the latter's invasion of the former. Its original name was Daecheong Hwangje Gongdeok Bi (大淸皇帝功德碑), which means the stele to the merits and virtues of the Emperor of the Great Qing. Initially erected at Samjeondo, near the Sambatnaru crossing point of the Han River in modern-day Seoul, it was thereafter buried and erected again several times. It is designated as the 101st historic site of South Korea.
wikipedia.extract_text: The Samjeondo Monument is a monument marking the submission of the Korean Joseon dynasty to the Manchu-led Qing dynasty in 1636 after the latter's invasion of the former. Its original name was Daecheong Hwangje Gongdeok Bi (大淸皇帝功德碑), which means the stele to the merits and virtues of the Emperor of the Great Qing. Initially erected at Samjeondo, near the Sambatnaru crossing point of the Han River in modern-day Seoul, it was thereafter buried and erected again several times. It is designated as the 101st historic site of South Korea.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: Description[edit] Both the Qing and Joseon dynasties saw the inscription as the litmus test for the latter's attitude toward the Qing emperor, so King Injo ensured that it flattered the Qing dynasty: the inscription narrates how the king of Joseon came to attach himself to the virtue of the Qing emperor from a Joseon point of view. Although one-sided, it provides a concise account of the Qing-Joseon relationship. The inscription starts with the description of the Qing campaign against Joseon in 1636. The Qing army besieged the Namhan fortress, where King Injo took refuge. He admitted his guilt, accepted the imperial edict and surrendered at Samjeondo. Since Hong Taiji felt compassion for the Joseon king, he mercifully sent the king back to the capital and rapidly withdrew the army without doing harm to the people. In the next paragraph, the inscription traces the history back to the Battle of Sarhū in 1619. The Joseon army, led by Gang Hong-rip, put on the appearance of supporting the Ming dynasty but surrendered to the Qing dynasty. However, all of the soldiers except the high-ranking ones were released by Nurhaci, and the inscription emphasizes the merciful act. Since Joseon still displayed disobedient behavior, Hong Taiji commenced the Later Jin invasion of Joseon in 1627. He did not overthrow the kingdom but established a Confucian "elder brother-younger brother" relationship. The inscription then goes on to describe the second campaign. When Hong Taiji proclaimed the Qing dynasty in 1636, Joseon did not accept it even though Qing China announced a war. The inscription stressed his benevolent acts during the war. Next, the inscription explains the background of erection of the monument. It says that the king voluntarily erected the monument at Samjeondo to let the excellent virtue of the Qing emperor be known around the world. Finally, the inscription summarizes the entire course of events in verse.[1] ^ .mw-parser-output cite.citation{font-style:inherit;word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output .citation query: The Hanging Temple, also known as Xuankong Temple, is a unique Buddhist temple built into a cliff near Mount Heng in Shanxi Province, China. It integrates elements of Buddhism, Taoism, and Confucianism and has a history of over 1,400 years.
answer:
The **Hanging Temple**, also known as **Xuankong Temple**, is a remarkable Buddhist temple located in Hunyuan County, near Mount Heng in Shanxi Province, China. Here are some key details about this unique attraction:

### Overview
- **Name:** Hanging Temple (悬空寺)
- **Location:** Near Mount Heng, Hunyuan County, Datong City, Shanxi Province, China
- **History:** The temple was built over 1,500 years ago and is notable for its precarious location on a sheer cliff. It integrates elements of Buddhism, Taoism, and Confucianism, reflecting the harmonious coexistence of these philosophies in Chinese culture.
- **Structure:** The temple is supported by wooden beams that are fitted into holes chiseled into the cliffs, with the main supportive structure hidden within the bedrock. It hangs approximately 75 meters (246 feet) above the ground.

### Historical Significance
The Hanging Temple is one of the main tourist attractions in the Datong area, alongside the Yungang Grottoes. It is renowned for its architectural ingenuity and scenic location, making it a popular site for visitors.

### Visual Tags
- **Tags:** mountain, temple, China, exterior, panoramic, aerial, sunny, valley
- **Popularity:** The temple is a well-visited site, attracting many tourists each year.

### Additional Information
- **Wikipedia Page:** [Hanging Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanging_Temple)
- **Wikidata ID:** [Q440976444](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q440976444)

If you're interested in visiting or learning more about the Hanging Temple, it offers a unique glimpse into the blend of religious traditions and stunning architectural design.

wikipedia.title: 悬空寺
wikipedia.extract: The Hanging Temple, also Hengshan Hanging Temple, Hanging Monastery or Xuankong Temple is a temple built into a cliff near Mount Heng in Hunyuan County, Datong City, Shanxi Province, China. The closest city is Datong, 64 kilometres (40 mi) to the northwest. Along with the Yungang Grottoes, the Hanging Temple is one of the main tourist attractions and historical sites in the Datong area. Built more than 1,500 years ago, this temple is notable not only for its location on a sheer precipice but also because as a Buddhist temple it also contains references to the other two of the three Chinese traditional philosophies or religions (三教): Taoism, and Confucianism. The structure is kept in place with oak crossbeams fitted into holes chiseled into the cliffs. The main supportive structure is hidden inside the bedrock. The monastery is located in the small canyon basin, and the body of the building hangs from the middle of the cliff under the prominent summit, protecting the temple from rain erosion and sunlight bake.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] According to legend, construction of the temple was started at the end of the Northern Wei dynasty by only one man, a monk named Liaoran (了然) in 491 AD. Hanging Temple, located in Hunyuan County, Datong City, Shanxi Province, China, is a temple integrating Confucianism, Buddhism, and Taoism. It has a history of more than 1,400 years.[1] The entire temple was built into a cliff face on the west side of Jinxia Gorge, approximately 75 meters (246 feet) above the ground. It relies on 27 wooden beams to support all the main temple buildings. The temple is also reinforced with iron chains and beams to enhance its stability. From a distance, it looks like it is hanging in the air. As early as Tuoba Tao, the third emperor of the Northern Wei Dynasty, he proposed to build temples in the north. Emperor Taiwu once "abolished Buddhism" and "destroyed Buddhism", but later repented and "promoted Buddhism" and "promoted Taoism". During the Southern and Northern Dynasties, Chinese Taoism was divided into northern and southern Taoist temples. Emperor Xiaowen Tuoba Yuanhong saw the majesty of the Buddhist temples in Luoyang and wanted to build Buddhist and Taoist temples in the north. He came up with a unique idea, found a Taoist priest, and ordered to build a "Xuankong Temple" on the cliff halfway up Mount Hengshan, which could not reach the sky or the ground.[2] ^ sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Overview[edit] The entire 40 halls and pavilions are all built on cliffs which are over 30 metres (98 ft) from the ground. The distance from north to south is longer than from east to west and it becomes higher and higher from the gate in the south to north along the mountain. The temple can be divided into a northern and southern section. Northern section[edit] The northern section contains:[1] Wufo Hall - The Hall of the Five Tathagatas Guanyin Hall - Hall of the bodhisattva Guanyin Hall of Three Religions (三教殿). The Hall of Three Religions mainly enshrines Buddhist deities as well as both Taoism and Confucianism. The statues of Śakyamuni (middle), Lao-Tze (left) and Confucius (right) are enshrined in the hall. This reflects the prevailing idea of "Three Teaching Harmonious as One" (三教合流) in the Ming and Qing dynasties (1368–1911).[1] Southern section[edit] The southern part has three floors, it contains the following halls:[1] Chunyang Palace - for worshiping Lü Dongbin - one of the Eight Immortals of Taoism Sanguan Hall (Hall of the Three Officials, 三官殿) - the largest hall in the temple, in which the "Three Great Emperor-Officials" (the officials of Heaven, Earth and Water) are worshiped with Ming era clay sculptures. Leiyin Hall (Thunder Hall) - A Buddhist hall dedicated to Buddha Śakyamuni located at the top of the southern section. ^ a b c .mw-parser-output wikipedia.title: 悬空寺
wikipedia.extract: The Hanging Temple, also Hengshan Hanging Temple, Hanging Monastery or Xuankong Temple is a temple built into a cliff near Mount Heng in Hunyuan County, Datong City, Shanxi Province, China. The closest city is Datong, 64 kilometres (40 mi) to the northwest. Along with the Yungang Grottoes, the Hanging Temple is one of the main tourist attractions and historical sites in the Datong area. Built more than 1,500 years ago, this temple is notable not only for its location on a sheer precipice but also because as a Buddhist temple it also contains references to the other two of the three Chinese traditional philosophies or religions (三教): Taoism, and Confucianism. The structure is kept in place with oak crossbeams fitted into holes chiseled into the cliffs. The main supportive structure is hidden inside the bedrock. The monastery is located in the small canyon basin, and the body of the building hangs from the middle of the cliff under the prominent summit, protecting the temple from rain erosion and sunlight bake.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History[edit] According to legend, construction of the temple was started at the end of the Northern Wei dynasty by only one man, a monk named Liaoran (了然) in 491 AD. Hanging Temple, located in Hunyuan County, Datong City, Shanxi Province, China, is a temple integrating Confucianism, Buddhism, and Taoism. It has a history of more than 1,400 years.[1] The entire temple was built into a cliff face on the west side of Jinxia Gorge, approximately 75 meters (246 feet) above the ground. It relies on 27 wooden beams to support all the main temple buildings. The temple is also reinforced with iron chains and beams to enhance its stability. From a distance, it looks like it is hanging in the air. As early as Tuoba Tao, the third emperor of the Northern Wei Dynasty, he proposed to build temples in the north. Emperor Taiwu once "abolished Buddhism" and "destroyed Buddhism", but later repented and "promoted Buddhism" and "promoted Taoism". During the Southern and Northern Dynasties, Chinese Taoism was divided into northern and southern Taoist temples. Emperor Xiaowen Tuoba Yuanhong saw the majesty of the Buddhist temples in Luoyang and wanted to build Buddhist and Taoist temples in the north. He came up with a unique idea, found a Taoist priest, and ordered to build a "Xuankong Temple" on the cliff halfway up Mount Hengshan, which could not reach the sky or the ground.[2] ^ sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Overview[edit] The entire 40 halls and pavilions are all built on cliffs which are over 30 metres (98 ft) from the ground. The distance from north to south is longer than from east to west and it becomes higher and higher from the gate in the south to north along the mountain. The temple can be divided into a northern and southern section. Northern section[edit] The northern section contains:[1] Wufo Hall - The Hall of the Five Tathagatas Guanyin Hall - Hall of the bodhisattva Guanyin Hall of Three Religions (三教殿). The Hall of Three Religions mainly enshrines Buddhist deities as well as both Taoism and Confucianism. The statues of Śakyamuni (middle), Lao-Tze (left) and Confucius (right) are enshrined in the hall. This reflects the prevailing idea of "Three Teaching Harmonious as One" (三教合流) in the Ming and Qing dynasties (1368–1911).[1] Southern section[edit] The southern part has three floors, it contains the following halls:[1] Chunyang Palace - for worshiping Lü Dongbin - one of the Eight Immortals of Taoism Sanguan Hall (Hall of the Three Officials, 三官殿) - the largest hall in the temple, in which the "Three Great Emperor-Officials" (the officials of Heaven, Earth and Water) are worshiped with Ming era clay sculptures. Leiyin Hall (Thunder Hall) - A Buddhist hall dedicated to Buddha Śakyamuni located at the top of the southern section. ^ a b c .mw-parser-output He came up with a unique idea, found a Taoist priest, and ordered to build a "Xuankong Temple" on the cliff halfway up Mount Hengshan, which could not reach the sky or the ground.[2] ^
